RESERVED FOR ORDERS ON 12.03.2021, THIS DAY, THE COURT
PRONOUNCED THE FOLLOWING:


                              ORDER

This petition is filed under Section 482 of Cr.P.C, praying this Court to quash the complaint dated 19.12.2019 (Annexure- A) and FIR dated 19.12.2019 (Annexure-A1) in Crime No.122/2019 on the file of the VII Additional Civil Judge (Jr.Dn.) and JMFC, Mysuru, for the offences punishable under Sections 378 and 380 of IPC and grant such other relief as deems fit in the circumstances of the case.

2. The factual matrix of the case is that the complainant/respondent No.2 has filed a complaint on 12.12.2019 making the allegation in the complaint that he was working in the petitioners' institution from 2009 to 2015 and he was having the documents pertaining to the Tourism Department. From the beginning of 2015, differences were 4 arisen between him and the petitioners institution. Hence, he gave resignation on 05.01.2015. The respondent No.2 was requested to continue till the completion of the academic year and he agreed for the same and in the month of May he gave the resignation and the Management did not accept the same. That on 19.05.2015 and 20.05.2015, he was on leave to receive the Doctorate in Literature for his book "Karnataka A Delight For Tourist" which he had written and Belagavi Rani Chennamma University gave the Doctorate and while going to receive the said Doctorate, he locked his room. In his absence that on 20.05.2015, these petitioners removed the lock and entered the room and stole the documents, letter heads, receipts, bills and vouchers without his consent. The petitioners institution with malafide intention and on personal vengeance removed the documents and now they made an allegation against the complainant that he has misappropriated the amount.

3. It is also alleged in the complaint that though other staff witnessed the said incident, they are not coming forward to give statement. The police investigated the matter against the case registered against him and filed the charge-sheet. During the course of investigation in the case registered against 5 respondent No.2/complainant, it is categorically admitted that they have removed the documents and also not drawn any mahazar and prima facie it discloses that they have committed the offence. Hence, requested to take action against the petitioners. Based on the complaint, the police have registered the case against the petitioners for the offences punishable under Sections 378 and 380 of IPC. Hence, the petitioners have approached this Court by filing this petition for seeking order of quashing.

4. The learned counsel for the petitioners in his arguments referring the brief synopsis which he has prepared, contended that respondent No.2 was appointed in 2005 and the institution introduced Tourism Department and respondent No.2 was made as Head of the said Department including collection of fees, admissions etc. A number of complaints were lodged in the year 2014 by the students/parents to the society against respondent No.2 about his misappropriation, misdeeds about admissions, etc. and ultimately an internal auditor was appointed. Respondent No.2 gave resignation on 05.01.2015 admitting guilt that he could not maintain proper accounts of the Department, but went on litigating against the 6 management/petitioners. The respondent No.2 filed defamation case against the petitioners and the society also lodged complaint against him on 01.11.2015 and in the local newspaper 'Star of Mysore', the same was appeared and hence respondent No.2 filed a private complaint against the petitioners for the offences punishable under Sections 409 and 500 of IPC and the same was quashed by this Court. It is also the contention of the petitioners that civil suit in O.S.No.17/2016 filed by the petitioners against respondent No.2 is pending, claiming misappropriated amount of Rs.3 Crores and odd. The respondent No.2 also filed written statement in the suit, but not stated anything about the present offence of theft and civil suit for recovery is pending.

5. The learned counsel for the petitioners would vehemently contend that Crime No.65/2015 has been investigated and the police have filed the charge-sheet. Now respondent No.2 has lodged a theft case in 2019 though the alleged incident was taken place according to the complainant in the year 2015 and there is a delay in lodging the complaint. This complaint is nothing but off shoot of the civil suit and criminal case registered against him. In support of his 7 contentions, the learned counsel would vehemently contend that in the written statement filed by respondent No.2, he has not stated even one word about this offence of theft of documents and so also defamation case was also quashed and nothing is whispered about the present offence of theft of 2015. The complaint lodged by respondent No.2 is clear that he was not in station at the time of alleged offence and only he is relying upon hearsay complaint and also stated that he had thought of not lodging the complaint as he was aged about 68 years and only with dishonest intention, the present complaint is filed. The FIR is lodged by the police mechanically without application of mind and there was a delay in lodging the complaint. It is also contended that in the earlier proceedings either filed by respondent No.2 against the petitioners or filed by the petitioners against respondent No.2, has not said even one word about the said alleged theft. As per Bye-law No.13.6 of the Mahajana Education Society, the Secretary shall be the custodian of all records such as cheque books, pass books, receipt books, day books, cash register and other relevant and confidential documents. Therefore, respondent No.2 being an 8 employee of the institution cannot lodge a complaint by saying that the documents are stolen from his legal custody.

6. The learned counsel for the petitioners in support of his contentions, relied upon the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of STATE OF HARYANA AND OTHERS v. CH.

BHAJAN LAL AND OTHERS reported in AIR 1992 SC 604(1) and brought to the notice of this Court Sections 154(1) and 157(1) of Cr.P.C. He also brought to the notice of this Court seven guidelines for entertaining the petition in High Court exercising the powers under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. Particularly he relied upon the first, fifth and seventh guidelines of the said judgment.

7. The learned counsel also relied upon the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of DALIP KAUR AND OTHERS v. JAGNAR SINGH AND ANOTHER reported in (2009) 14 SCC 696, wherein it is held that where allegations contained in FIR, even if given face value and taken to be correct, do not disclose commission of the alleged offence and disclose only a civil dispute, FIR is liable to be quashed.

9

8. The learned counsel also relied upon the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of KISHAN SINGH (DEAD) THROUGH LRS. v. GURPAL SINGH AND OTHERS reported in (2010) 3 SCC (Cri) 1091 and brought to the notice of this Court paragraph No.25 of the judgment. It is also held with regard to exercising of power under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. regarding large delay in lodging the complaint and malafide proceedings launched to wreak vengeance, proceedings has to be quashed.

9. The learned counsel also relied upon the judgment of this Court in the case of MRS. INDIRA POOVAIAH AND ANOTHER v. THE STATE OF KARNATAKA AND ANOTHER reported in 2018 (2) Kar.L.R. 864 and brought to the notice of this Court paragraph No.11. In the said judgment, it is discussed with regard to scope of Section 482 of Cr.P.C. Inherent powers of the High Court for quashing of complaint. Frustrated litigant who has failed in civil Court attempts to invoke criminal jurisdiction with malafide intention or with a motive of wreaking vengeance on the present accused - Civil litigations pending or disposed of - amounts to abuse of process of Court.

10

10. The learned counsel also relied upon the judgment of this Court in the case of V. NAGABHUSHAN AND OTHERS v. M/S. N.K. CONSTRUCTIONS, BENGALURU AND ANOTHER reported in 2019 (1) KCCR 543 and brought to the notice of this Court paragraph Nos.3, 4 and 9. It is also observed that when the civil suits are pending between the rival parties, proceedings has to be quashed.

11. The learned counsel also relied upon the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of SARDAR ALI KHAN v. STATE OF UTTAR PRADESH THROUGH PRINCIPAL SECRETARY HOME DEPARTMENT AND ANOTHER reported in AIR 2020 SC 626 and brought to the notice of this Court paragraph No.9, wherein the Apex Court discussed with regard to the pendency of the civil suit and complaint filed alleging forgery and impersonation regarding validity of sale deed and when the same is pending before the civil suit for cancellation of sale deed having regard to serious factual disputes which are of civil nature, continuation of criminal proceedings during pendency of civil suit is nothing but an abuse of process of law.

11

12. The learned counsel also relied upon the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of AHMAD ALI QURAISHI AND ANOTHER v. STATE OF UTTAR PRADESH AND ANOTHER reported in AIR 2020 SC 788 and brought to the notice of this Court paragraph Nos.20 to 24. The Apex Court also discussed with regard to where civil disputes are pending regarding property between the parties and criminal proceedings maliciously instituted with ulterior motives - permitting which would be abuse of process of Court and held that proceedings are liable to be quashed.

13. Per contra, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 would vehemently contend that subsequent to stealing of the original documents breaking open the lock of the room in which it was kept and in the custody of respondent No.2, from the day one the complainant is agitating the same and in the complaint, specific reasons are stated for delay in lodging the complaint. It is also contended that the theft of documents were taken place within the vicinity of the petitioners institution and no official came forward to help respondent No.2 and respondent No.2 reiterated the same subsequent to the incident and the very contention that the same has not to been attributed in any 12 subsequent proceedings cannot be accepted. It is also the contention of the learned counsel that the same has to be emerged during the course of investigation in connection with the case registered against respondent No.2 by the institution and in each and every stage he has pointed out the theft of the documents which were in his custody and now the final report is filed and case has been registered against him for misappropriation and civil suit is also filed claiming the amount of Rs.3 Crores and odd against respondent No.2 herein.

14. The learned counsel in support of his arguments brought to the notice of this Court the statement of objections filed by him and in detail controverted the allegations made in the petition. The learned counsel also brought to the notice of this Court that in the bail application dated 06.11.2015 he has stated in paragraph No.14 that on 20.05.2015, the President and the Secretary went to the Department premises situated at Metagalli and took custody of all the papers, documents, record books and sealed the chamber of the petitioner. The learned counsel brought to the notice of this Court that the complaint dated 28.12.2016 was given to the Commissioner of Police, 13 Mysore City, Mysore, wherein categorical allegations are made that with the sole intention to frame respondent No.2 in the said case, Mr. Bhagawat's wife and father-in-law broke upon the chamber on 20.05.2015 when he was on leave and took away all the receipts, vouchers, record books etc. kept in his office. Now they have charged him for not maintaining the records of the expenses.

15. The learned counsel also brought to the notice of this Court when he was summoned and enquired in connection with Crime No.65/2015, he reiterated the same in his statement before the police on 25.01.2017. The learned counsel brought to the notice of this Court that he gave the explanation to the Investigating Officer, City Crime Branch, reiterating the same and also brought to the notice of this Court Annexure-R9 wherein he gave response to the Inspector of Police. He has reiterated that when he was on leave on 19.5.2015 and 20.05.2015, the petitioners have barged into his room and removed the vouchers, bills and other documents.

16. The learned counsel also brought to the notice of this Court Annexure-R10 which was given to the City Crime Branch. In the reply dated 21.05.2018, the incident has been culled out 14 and explained the same. The learned counsel also brought to the notice of this Court the questionnaire to the Secretary of the petitioners institution which was recorded in connection with Crime No.65/2015, wherein the Secretary categorically admitted that the Management has taken possession of all the records and documents and also categorically admitted that there was no concurrence of respondent No.2 in taking the documents. In the enquiry also categorically stated that they have not conducted any mahazar for having taken the documents and in the questionnaire, categorically admitted that some records were taken for verification. Hence, it is clear that they have barged into the room of respondent No.2 and took away all the relevant documents and subsequently registered the criminal case and also filed the civil suit for recovery of amount of Rs.3 Crores and odd.

17. The learned counsel for respondent No.2 in support of his arguments relied upon the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of PYARE LAL BHARGAVA v. THE STATE OF RAJASTHAN reported in AIR 1963 SC 1094 and brought to the notice of this Court paragraph No.8 of the judgment, wherein it is observed that the facts found were that the appellant got 15 the file between December 15 and 16, 1948, to his house, made it available to Ram Kumar Ram and on December 16, 1948 returned it to the office. On these facts it is contended that the prosecution has not made out that the appellant dishonestly took any movable property within the meaning of Section 378 of the IPC. The Apex Court also discussed with regard to A, a superintendent in Government office taking a certain file from office to his house and making the same available to B and then returning the same after replacing certain papers by other papers, to office. A held was not in legal possession of the file. To commit theft one need not take movable property permanently out of the possession of another with the intention not to return it to him. A unlawfully stole the file from the department, and for a short time he deprived the Head of the Department of the possession of the said file. A temporary period of deprivation or dispossession of the property of another causes loss to the other person. A person acts dishonestly if he temporarily dispossesses another of his property. A's case therefore fell within four corners of Section 378 of IPC.

18. The learned counsel also relied upon the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of PRITI SARAF AND ANOTHER v. 16 STATE OF NCT OF DELHI AND ANOTHER reported in 2021 SCC online SC 206, wherein the Apex Court set aside the order passed by the High Court in quashing the criminal proceedings and restored the complaint making an observation that the High Court has failed to consider the charge-sheet and other materials available on record and the very observation of the High Court that it was a simple case of termination because of breach of terms of contract giving rise to a purely civil dispute or initiation of the arbitral proceedings would not attract the provisions under Sections 406, 420, 34 of IPC may not hold good at this stage for the reason what is being suggested by the learned counsel for respondent No.2 can be his defence during the course of trial but was not open to be examined by the High Court to take a judicial notice and for quashing of the criminal proceedings in exercise of its inherent powers under Section 482 of Cr.P.C.

19. Having heard the learned counsel for the petitioners and learned counsel for respondent No.2 and also considering the principles laid down in the judgments referred supra, this Court has to examine whether it is a fit case to exercise the powers under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. to quash the FIR. On perusal of the complaint, an allegation is made that in the 17 absence of the complainant, the petitioners herein have broke open the lock and barged into the room, which was provided to the complainant by the institution of the petitioners and stole the documents, letter heads, receipts, bills and vouchers without his consent. No doubt, there is a delay in lodging the complaint. The incident was taken place according to the complainant on 20.05.2015 and the complaint is lodged in 2019. The learned counsel for the petitioners brought to the notice of this Court that there is no any averment in the written statement that in the civil suit filed against respondent No.2 with regard to this incident and nowhere stated with regard to the incident is concerned. The said contention cannot be accepted for the reason that the learned counsel for respondent No.2 brought to the notice of this Court in detail, which has been referred supra that respondent No.2 brought to the notice of the Investigating Officer, who has investigated the matter that the case is registered against respondent No.2 herein. The Court also cannot expect the same in the written statement with regard to civil suit filed against him. It is the specific case of respondent No.2 that by removing the documents, vouchers etc., the 18 petitioners filed the criminal case and also civil suit for recovery of more than Rs.3 Crores.

20. It is also brought to the notice of this Court that when investigation was conducted by the police in respect of the case registered against respondent No.2 herein, the Secretary of the Institution categorically admitted in terms of Annexure-R11 when a question was put has the Management taken possession of all the records and documents of the MTDI, the answer was given that some records which was available for verification was taken in possession and no concurrence was given by respondent No.2. It is further admitted that the official mahazar was not conducted and some records were taken for verification, Hence, it is clear that the incident was taken place and specific allegation that the documents were stolen, prima facie discloses in Annexure-R11. The specific allegations were made in the complaint that the petitioners barged into the room in which the complainant had kept the documents which were in his custody and stole the documents.

21. Having taken note of the complaint averments and also the relevant materials available before the Court as pointed 19 by the learned counsel for respondent No.2 and also the records discloses that even after the registration of the case against respondent No.2 in the bail application and also in reply to the Investigating Officer specifically contended with regard to incident is concerned. It is also the case of the complainant that the documents which were in his custody were removed and thereafter cases are instituted against him, both criminal case as well as civil case. Under the circumstances, the very contention of the learned counsel for the petitioners that there cannot be any criminal prosecution against the petitioners cannot be accepted and the materials found before the Court prima facie discloses with regard to the incident was taken place, that too in the absence of respondent No.2. The very contention of the petitioners that the complainant came to know about the incident through other officials and the same is a hearsay complaint, cannot be decided at this juncture and the Investigating Officer has to probe the matter and unearth the crime. The High Court should not venture to prevent the Investigating Officer in conducting the investigation. May be there is a delay in lodging the complaint, but the fact is that the documents which were in custody of respondent No.2 were taken 20 away. The Apex Court in the judgment in the case of Pyare Lal Bhargave (supra) has held that even if the documents are removed for temporary purpose, it amounts to invoking the ingredients of Section 378 of IPC. Under the circumstances, I do not find any merit in the petition to quash the FIR. It requires further investigation.

22. In view of the discussions made above, I pass the following:

ORDER The petition is rejected.

incident through other officials and the same is a hearsay
complaint, cannot be decided at this juncture and the
Investigating Officer has to probe the matter and unearth the
crime. The High Court should not venture to prevent the
Investigating Officer in conducting the investigation. May be
there is a delay in lodging the complaint, but the fact is that the
documents which were in custody of respondent No.2 were taken away. The Apex Court in the judgment in the case of Pyare Lal
Bhargave (supra) has held that even if the documents are
removed for temporary purpose, it amounts to invoking the
ingredients of Section 378 of IPC. Under the circumstances, I do
not find any merit in the petition to quash the FIR. It requires
further investigation.

precedent_analysis:
BHAJAN LAL AND OTHERS reported in AIR 1992 SC 604(1)
and brought to the notice of this Court Sections 154(1) and 157(1) of Cr.P.C. He also brought to the notice of this Court
seven guidelines for entertaining the petition in High Court
exercising the powers under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. Particularly
he relied upon the first, fifth and seventh guidelines of the said
judgment.
The learned counsel also relied upon the judgment of
the Apex Court in the case of DALIP KAUR AND OTHERS v.
JAGNAR SINGH AND ANOTHER reported in (2009) 14 SCC
696, wherein it is held that where allegations contained in FIR,
even if given face value and taken to be correct, do not disclose
commission of the alleged offence and disclose only a civil
dispute, FIR is liable to be quashed.
The learned counsel also relied upon the judgment of
the Apex Court in the case of KISHAN SINGH (DEAD)
THROUGH LRS. v. GURPAL SINGH AND OTHERS reported in
(2010) 3 SCC (Cri) 1091 and brought to the notice of this
Court paragraph No.25 of the judgment. It is also held with
regard to exercising of power under Section 482 of Cr.P.C.
regarding large delay in lodging the complaint and malafide
proceedings launched to wreak vengeance, proceedings has to
be quashed.
The learned counsel also relied upon the judgment of
this Court in the case of MRS. INDIRA POOVAIAH AND
ANOTHER v. THE STATE OF KARNATAKA AND ANOTHER reported in 2018 (2) Kar.L.R. 864 and brought to the notice of
this Court paragraph No.11. In the said judgment , it is
discussed with regard to scope of Section 482 of Cr.P.C.
Inherent powers of the High Court for quashing of complaint.
Frustrated litigant who has failed in civil Court attempts to
invoke criminal jurisdiction with malafide intention or with a
motive of wreaking vengeance on the present accused - Civil
litigations pending or disposed of - amounts to abuse of process
of Court.
The learned counsel also relied upon the judgment of
this Court in the case of V. NAGABHUSHAN AND OTHERS v.
M/S. N.K. CONSTRUCTIONS, BENGALURU AND ANOTHER reported in 2019 (1) KCCR 543 and brought to the notice of
this Court paragraph Nos.3, 4 and 9. It is also observed that
when the civil suits are pending between the rival parties,
proceedings has to be quashed.
The learned counsel also relied upon the judgment of
the Apex Court in the case of SARDAR ALI KHAN v. STATE OF
UTTAR PRADESH THROUGH PRINCIPAL SECRETARY HOME
DEPARTMENT AND ANOTHER reported in AIR 2020 SC 626
and brought to the notice of this Court paragraph No.9, wherein
the Apex Court discussed with regard to the pendency of the civil
suit and complaint filed alleging forgery and impersonation
regarding validity of sale deed and when the same is pending
before the civil suit for cancellation of sale deed having regard to
serious factual disputes which are of civil nature, continuation of
criminal proceedings during pendency of civil suit is nothing but
an abuse of process of law.
The learned counsel also relied upon the judgment of
the Apex Court in the case of AHMAD ALI QURAISHI AND
ANOTHER v. STATE OF UTTAR PRADESH AND ANOTHER reported in AIR 2020 SC 788 and brought to the notice of this
Court paragraph Nos.20 to 24. The Apex Court also discussed
with regard to where civil disputes are pending regarding
property between the parties and criminal proceedings
maliciously instituted with ulterior motives - permitting which
would be abuse of process of Court and held that proceedings
are liable to be quashed.
The learned counsel for respondent No.2 in support
of his arguments relied upon the judgment of the Apex Court in
the case of PYARE LAL BHARGAVA v. THE STATE OF
RAJASTHAN reported in AIR 1963 SC 1094 and brought to
the notice of this Court paragraph No.8 of the judgment, wherein
it is observed that the facts found were that the appellant got the file between December 15 and 16, 1948, to his house, made
it available to Ram Kumar Ram and on December 16, 1948
returned it to the office. On these facts it is contended that the
prosecution has not made out that the appellant dishonestly took
any movable property within the meaning of Section 378 of the
IPC. The Apex Court also discussed with regard to A, a
superintendent in Government office taking a certain file from
office to his house and making the same available to B and then
returning the same after replacing certain papers by other
papers, to office. A held was not in legal possession of the file.
To commit theft one need not take movable property
permanently out of the possession of another with the intention
not to return it to him. A unlawfully stole the file from the
department, and for a short time he deprived the Head of the
Department of the possession of the said file. A temporary
period of deprivation or dispossession of the property of another
causes loss to the other person. A person acts dishonestly if he
temporarily dispossesses another of his property. A's case
therefore fell within four corners of Section 378 of IPC.
The learned counsel also relied upon the judgment of
the Apex Court in the case of PRITI SARAF AND ANOTHER v. STATE OF NCT OF DELHI AND ANOTHER reported in 2021
SCC online SC 206, wherein the Apex Court set aside the order
passed by the High Court in quashing the criminal proceedings
and restored the complaint making an observation that the High
Court has failed to consider the charge-sheet and other materials
available on record and the very observation of the High Court
that it was a simple case of termination because of breach of
terms of contract giving rise to a purely civil dispute or initiation
of the arbitral proceedings would not attract the provisions under
Sections 406, 420, 34 of IPC may not hold good at this stage for
the reason what is being suggested by the learned counsel for
respondent No.2 can be his defence during the course of trial but
was not open to be examined by the High Court to take a judicial
notice and for quashing of the criminal proceedings in exercise of
its inherent powers under Section 482 of Cr.P.C.
court_reasoning:
The learned counsel in support of his arguments
brought to the notice of this Court the statement of objections
filed by him and in detail controverted the allegations made in
the petition. The learned counsel also brought to the notice of
this Court that in the bail application dated 06.11.2015 he has
stated in paragraph No.14 that on 20.05.2015, the President and
the Secretary went to the Department premises situated at
Metagalli and took custody of all the papers, documents, record
books and sealed the chamber of the petitioner. The learned
counsel brought to the notice of this Court that the complaint
dated 28.12.2016 was given to the Commissioner of Police, Mysore City, Mysore, wherein categorical allegations are made
that with the sole intention to frame respondent No.2 in the said
case, Mr. Bhagawat's wife and father-in-law broke upon the
chamber on 20.05.2015 when he was on leave and took away all
the receipts, vouchers, record books etc. kept in his office. Now
they have charged him for not maintaining the records of the
expenses.
The learned counsel also brought to the notice of this
Court when he was summoned and enquired in connection with
Crime No.65/2015, he reiterated the same in his statement
before the police on 25.01.2017. The learned counsel brought to
the notice of this Court that he gave the explanation to the
Investigating Officer, City Crime Branch, reiterating the same
and also brought to the notice of this Court Annexure-R9
wherein he gave response to the Inspector of Police. He has
reiterated that when he was on leave on 19.5.2015 and
05.2015, the petitioners have barged into his room and
removed the vouchers, bills and other documents.
The learned counsel also brought to the notice of this
Court Annexure-R10 which was given to the City Crime Branch.
In the reply dated 21.05.2018, the incident has been culled out and explained the same. The learned counsel also brought to the
notice of this Court the questionnaire to the Secretary of the
petitioners institution which was recorded in connection with
Crime No.65/2015, wherein the Secretary categorically admitted
that the Management has taken possession of all the records and
documents and also categorically admitted that there was no
concurrence of respondent No.2 in taking the documents. In the
enquiry also categorically stated that they have not conducted
any mahazar for having taken the documents and in the
questionnaire, categorically admitted that some records were
taken for verification. Hence, it is clear that they have barged
into the room of respondent No.2 and took away all the relevant
documents and subsequently registered the criminal case and
also filed the civil suit for recovery of amount of Rs.3 Crores and
odd.
Having heard the learned counsel for the petitioners
and learned counsel for respondent No.2 and also considering
the principles laid down in the judgments referred supra, this
Court has to examine whether it is a fit case to exercise the
powers under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. to quash the FIR. On
perusal of the complaint, an allegation is made that in the absence of the complainant, the petitioners herein have broke
open the lock and barged into the room, which was provided to
the complainant by the institution of the petitioners and stole the
documents, letter heads, receipts, bills and vouchers without his
consent. No doubt, there is a delay in lodging the complaint.
The incident was taken place according to the complainant on
05.2015 and the complaint is lodged in 2019. The learned
counsel for the petitioners brought to the notice of this Court
that there is no any averment in the written statement that in
the civil suit filed against respondent No.2 with regard to this
incident and nowhere stated with regard to the incident is
concerned. The said contention cannot be accepted for the
reason that the learned counsel for respondent No.2 brought to
the notice of this Court in detail, which has been referred supra
that respondent No.2 brought to the notice of the Investigating
Officer, who has investigated the matter that the case is
registered against respondent No.2 herein. The Court also
cannot expect the same in the written statement with regard to
civil suit filed against him. It is the specific case of respondent
No.2 that by removing the documents, vouchers etc., the petitioners filed the criminal case and also civil suit for recovery
of more than Rs.3 Crores.
It is also brought to the notice of this Court that
when investigation was conducted by the police in respect of the
case registered against respondent No.2 herein, the Secretary of
the Institution categorically admitted in terms of Annexure-R11
when a question was put has the Management taken possession
of all the records and documents of the MTDI, the answer was
given that some records which was available for verification was
taken in possession and no concurrence was given by
respondent No.2. It is further admitted that the official mahazar
was not conducted and some records were taken for verification,
Hence, it is clear that the incident was taken place and specific
allegation that the documents were stolen, prima facie discloses
in Annexure-R11. The specific allegations were made in the
complaint that the petitioners barged into the room in which the
complainant had kept the documents which were in his custody
and stole the documents.

In view of the discussions made above, I pass the
following: ORDER
The petition is rejected. Sd/- JUDGE

case_summary: The complainant, Sri B.J. Puttaswamy, alleged that the accused, Sri N. Hanumegowda, made defamatory statements against him by filing multiple false complaints to various authorities, alleging illegal land grabbing, misuse of powers, and corruption against Puttaswamy. The complainant argued that these actions were intended to damage his reputation and were made with malicious intent. The dispute centered around a 10-acre land granted by the Government of Karnataka to the Vishwa Ganigara Samudaya Charitable Trust, of which Puttaswamy was the managing trustee. The accused claimed that the grant was illegal and made multiple complaints to various authorities, including the Land Grabbing Court, Anti-Corruption Bureau, and other government departments, alleging impropriety in the acquisition and use of the land by the Trust.
case_decision: The court found that Sri N. Hanumegowda made false allegations against Sri B.J. Puttaswamy with the intent to defame him, as evidenced by multiple dismissed complaints and defamatory statements made to the media. The court determined that the accused failed to prove the truth of his claims or show that his actions were in the public interest. As a result, the court held that Hanumegowda was guilty of defamation under Section 500 of the IPC, affirming that his actions were intended to harm Puttaswamy’s reputation
punishment: Conviction by first court. Fine and Imprisonment

Sri B.J.Puttaswamy vs Sri N.Hanumegowda on 6 November, 2019

 IN THE COURT OF LXXXI ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND
     SESSIONS JUDGE, BENGALURU (CCH82)

                       :Present :

   Sri RAMACHANDRA D. HUDDAR, B.Com., LLM.,
       LXXXI ACC & SJ, Bengaluru City (CCH-82)
           (Special Court exclusively to deal with
        criminal cases related to elected MPs/MLAs
                 in the State of Karnataka)


      Dated: This the 6th day of November, 2019

              Spl. CC No. 461 / 2018

COMPLAINANT:-         Sri B.J.Puttaswamy, MLC
                      Founder President /
                      Managing Trustee, Vishwa Ganigara
                      Samudaya Charitable Trust ®
                      r/o No.71, 4th Cross, 3rd Main
                      Rajmahal Vilas 2nd Stage
                      HIG Dollars Colony
                      Bengaluru-560 094

                      (Sri Keerthi     Hegde,    Advocate   for
                      Complainant)


                             V/s


ACCUSED:-             Sri N.Hanumegowda
                      r/a. 52/1, 2nd Cross, 3rd main Road
                      Kamakshipalya
                      Bangalore-560 079

                      (Smt.D.K.Sudarshini, Advocate)
                               2                 Spl.CC 461/2018

                     JUDGMENT

This case is arising out of a private complaint filed by complainant before the 8th ACMM, Bengaluru, which was registered as PCR No.1477/2018. After filing the complaint, said 8th ACMM, Bengaluru took cognizance of the offence and posted the case for recording sworn statement.

2. In view of establishment of this court as per Government Order No.LAW 10 LCE 2018 dt.8.2.2018 and notification of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka bearing No.GOB(I)1/2018, Dt.23.2.2018 exclusively to deal with criminal cases related to elected MPs/MLAs in the State of Karnataka, the entire records of this case are transmitted to this court and after transmission of the records, this case was re-numbered as PCR No.14/2018.

3. As the case was posted for recording sworn statement, complainant and his four witnesses gave their sworn statement before this court.

4. Learned predecessor of this court after hearing the arguments of counsel for the Complainant passed a 3 Spl.CC 461/2018 detailed order dt.3.7.2018 directing to register Special CC against the accused for the offence punishable U/s. 500 of IPC. Summons came to be issued against the accused for his appearance. Accordingly, accused appeared before this court and was enlarged on bail. Initially, accused appeared before this court i.e., party in person and thereafter he engaged a counsel to defend him.

5. Brief and relevant facts as set out by the Complainant in the complaint are as follows:-

"This private complaint is filed by the Complainant by invoking the provisions of Sec.199 r/w 200 of Cr.P.C., alleging that the Complainant is a Indian Citizen and resident of Bengaluru. He states that he is a social worker having dedicated his life for the past 40 years towards public service without any blemish remark against him. He further states that he was Member of Legislative Council and a former Minister of State of Karnataka. He enjoys political success and he is known to be a person of high integrity and moral statue and of unblemished character.
4 Spl.CC 461/2018 He also enjoys enormous good-will and reputation in the society.
It is further stated by the Complainant that he is also the President of Vishwa Ganigara Samudaya Charitable Trust which is being established for the betterment / improvement of Ganiga Community. The said Trust had proposed by means of an application to the Government of Karnataka for granting about 10 acres of land on long term lease basis. Accordingly, the Government of Karnataka has sanctioned 10 acres of land initially in Sy.No.112 of Nagaruru village, Dasanapura Hobli, Bengaluru North Taluk vide G.O.No.RD 367 LGB 2011 dated 20.9.2011 in favour of the Trust for 30 years on long term lease basis. Subsequently, said 10 acres of land was reduced to 08 acres of land dated 21.7.2015.
It is further stated by the Complainant that, the said Trust having taken possession of the land and has applied to the Nelamangala Development Authority for sanction of plan for putting up construction. Accordingly, said Nelamangala Development Authority issued sanction plan 5 Spl.CC 461/2018 vide order dt.19.10.2013 in favour of the Trust. The trust has paid Rs.18,07,600/- on 20.8.2013. To that effect a receipt came to be issued. The Trust also paid Rs.1,40,089/- to Dasanapura Grama Panchayath for sanction of plan for putting up construction work in the said property. Thus it is stated that the construction is well within the parameter of the sanction plan.
A specific allegation has been made by the Complainant that, though the accused knew all these factual factors, for the reasons best known to him, with an ulterior motive to extract money from the complainant, had lodged several false, frivolous and vexatious complaints. Likewise, he had filed complaint before the Karnataka Land Grabbing Prohibition Special Court. Said court after due enquiry passed an order dated 21.4.2017 and dismissed the complaint filed by the accused holding that there is no violation or land grabbing by the said Trust as alleged in the complaint lodged by the accused.
It is further specifically alleged that, the accused could not succeed before the Land Grabbing Court.
6 Spl.CC 461/2018 Thereafter, he approached Anti Corruption Bureau, Bengaluru on 27.4.2016 alleging that the Complainant has illegally acquired Government Gomala Land and has misued his powers being a public servant and got the above said land allotted in favour of Vishwa Ganigara Samudaya Charitable Trust. It is alleged in the said complaint that this complainant is very corrupt and has cheated the Government in various ways. Finally it is stated that the Complainant has illegally acquired all the lands with the help of the then chief Minister Sri B.S.Yedduyurappa and also with the help of other local authorities.
It is further alleged by the Complainant that, this accused also filed complaint before Deputy Commissioner, Bengaluru on 30.6.2016 questioning the allotment of land to Vishwa Ganigara Samudaya Charitable Trust. It is alleged that the said Trust has not met with basic criteria.
It is further stated by the Complainant that, the Anti Corruption Bureau, Bengaluru conducted detailed enquiry against all the false and baseless allegations made by the 7 Spl.CC 461/2018 accused and dismissed the complaint filed under Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 and issued endorsement on 8.9.2016. Specific assertions have been made by the Complainant that, due to the aforesaid enquiries by the LGC as well ACB and other public authorities, this Complainant has undergone huge amount of stress and humiliation in public life and this act of the accused is done with sole intention to defame his spotless reputation gained by the Complainant due to his work and perseverance. The accused with sole intention to extort money from the Complainant is trying to defame the spotless reputation gained by him. He further states that the accused is a habitual offender and under the guise of social service he filed these fraudulent cases before various authorities in order to arm-twist the innocent public servants for illegal monetary gain. The Public servants in order to protect their reputation in public paying huge sum though they have not committed any illegal activities. They pay the money to avoid unwanted defamation.
8 Spl.CC 461/2018 It is further stated by the Complainant that, he did not heed to the unwarranted pressure imposed by the accused for extracting money. He filed baseless complaint before Prl. Secretary, Revenue Department Karnataka on 11.7.2016 and also before Hon'ble Minister for Revenue, Karnataka on 28.6.2016. The concerned Departments have not raised any objections or charges against the Trust regarding any sort of illegality.
The Complainant states that, the allegations made by the accused in various complaints being filed by him is to make wrongful gain and to create bad impression in the minds of the public about the Complainant and to defame his image before the public, family and friends and disturb the regular activities of the said Trust which is functioning in a smooth manner.
It is further stated that, despite the baseless complaints being dismissed as false, the accused in order to harass the Complainant has once again filed another false complaint before Tahasildar, Nelamangala Taluk, Bengaluru rural district on 22.7.2017 not to effect katha, 9 Spl.CC 461/2018 pahani, etc., in relation to Sy.No.136/P4, New No.183 measuring 02 acres 14 guntas situated at Jakkanahalli village, Thyamagondlu Hobli, Nelamangala Tq., in favour of the Complainant. The accused has made defamatory remarks that the Complainant has not submitted the relevant documents to declare his assets and liabilities to Karnataka Lokayukta. It is enquired into and the complaint filed by the accused was dismissed. These series of complaints filed by the accused against the complainant, caused huge loss of reputation of the Complainant and damaged his good will.
It is further stated that, with sole malafide intention to extract money from the Complainant, these complaints have been filed by the accused. Complainant has religiously without any delay submitted his detailed assets and liabilities before Lokayukta.
It further alleged by the Complainant that, the accused approached the "Bangalore Mirror" news paper on 11.7.2016 to malign the reputation of the Complainant and furnished false information alleging several irregularities 10 Spl.CC 461/2018 of the Government in allotment of 10 acres of land to Vishwa Ganigara Samudaya Charitable Trust, Bengaluru, he alleged that the Complainant misused his powers being a public servant got the said land allotted in his favour. Though such complaints were already dismissed, the print media without proper verification have published false news paper on 11.7.2016. Due to this false information portrayed in the news paper, the Complainant has been severely defamed and he had to unnecessarily give clarification to all his friends and well wishers. No such illegal activity has taken place in getting the land allotted in favour of the Trust.
It is further stated that Vishwa Ganigara Samudaya Charitable Trust has constructed a multipurpose community hall for the welfare of the Ganiga Community. Even he has invited Chief Minister for the inauguration of the said community hall. But this accused in order to defame the Complainant addressed a rudimentary letter to the Deputy Commissioner of Bengaluru Urgan requesting him to withhold the inauguration ceremony of the 11 Spl.CC 461/2018 community hall built for Ganiga community alleging that the said community hall was constructed over the land illegally acquired by the Complainant. Because of the said act of the accused, the Hon'ble Chief Minister who supposed to attend the said function, but he did not attend. Thus the Complainant was put to humiliation before the public for no fault of his.
It is further alleged that the Complainant has not succumbed to the pressure tactics played by the accused. Accused did not stop his illegal activities, but he approached "Bengaluru Metropolitan Task Force' (referred to as BMTF for short) on 6.10.2017 on the issues stated supra. But the said complaint came to be dismissed.
It is further alleged by the Complainant that the accused has been lodging one or the other false and frivolous complaints before Tahasildar, Karnataka Lokayukta, ACB and such other authorities even though there is no truth in such complaints. Only in order to defame the Complainant's name, character and spoil his image in the minds of the public, family and friend circles, 12 Spl.CC 461/2018 these complaints have been filed by the accused with sole intention to extract money from Complainant.
The Complainant further states in the complaint that he is senior citizen aged 78 years. Due to this unlawful and dishonest activities of accused repeatedly filing false complaints one after the other, has affected the health of the Complainant and he was put to hardship mentally and physically.
In order to curb the illegal activities of the accused, this Complainant filed complaint before Sanjayanagara Police station against accused. In order to counter the said complaint, accused has filed false complaint before Kamakshipalya police station alleging that the Complainant is threatening him. The misdeeds of the accused was not limited to filing the complaint, he also approached the television and print media and professed the same lie. All the allegations made by the accused are false, baseless, vexatious and frivolous. Unfortunately, the TV Channels telecasted the said news with sole intention to malign the reputation of the Complainant. The accused is behind 13 Spl.CC 461/2018 telecasting of such news. As the said false news telecasted against the Complainant at the instance of the accused, the respect of the Complainant was seriously damaged. Telecast in the Television etc., not only maligned reputation of the Complainant, but also maligned the reputation of family of the Complainant.
It is stated that the Complainant and his family has earned the respect and reputation in the field of politics because of the hard work done by them. The accused by all his illegal means caused this telecast and publications in the print and electronic media, friends and relatives of Complainant residing various parts of Karnataka have started enquiring about the program being telecasted. The telecast does not bear any true facts, such telecast has caused loss of reputation of the Complainant.

20. So far as defamation is concerned, as a principle of equity, every man is entitled to have his reputation preserved intact. A man's reputation is his property and possibly more valuable than other properties, and any words calculated to infringe this right affords a good cause of action.

21. It is stated that "no man may disparage or destroy the reputation of another. Every man has a right to have his good name maintained unimpaired. This right is a jus in rem, a right absolute and good against all the world.

22. This cause of action for defamation has been recognized from the very beginning of our civilization, and people have been resorting to mutual fights to smoothen out the wrong done to their reputation.

23. Then what is defamation? From what has been stated above the question of defamation has been primary 27 Spl.CC 461/2018 linked up with one's reputation that one commands among one's fellow beings and it is the infringement of this right to have one's reputation preserved intact that gives the cause of action. Broadly speaking defamation may be defined as a false and damaging statement. Salmond has defined it as a wrong that consists in the publication of a false and defamatory statement respecting another without lawful justification. It is conventional to say that, defamation includes a statement concerning any person which exposes him to hatred, ridicule or contempt. But this statement is no longer considered as exhaustive. The best method of approach to the definition of defamation is to consider it from the point view of the right which the defamatory statement is alleged to infringe. No doubt one's reputation includes all the moral and material advantages to which it may entitle him in his relationship with the Society as a whole. One's reputation may be so well established that nothing said or done on the part of the accused could harm it but still the accused would be liable not because he had harmed the plaintiff's reputation 28 Spl.CC 461/2018 but for his deprived intention and his tendency to cause harm.

In criminal cases however truth of the statements alleged to be defamatory is only a defence when the truth has come out for public good. In India, this law is enacted In Indian Penal Code. Exception 1 to Sec.499 of the Indian Penal Code is culled out above says it is not defamation to impute anything which is true concerning any person, if it be for public good that the imputation should be made or published. Whether or not it is for the public good is a question of fact.

29. The burden of proving that the words alleged to be defamatory are true is on the accused, and the burden of proof on this point is not shifted nor does the presumption of good conduct cease to be available in 33 Spl.CC 461/2018 favour of the Complainant in consequence of his having given evidence on this behalf. In the cases of criminal defamation, the accused has not only to justify the whole of his libel but the plea taken has to be proved as strictly as if the complainant was being prosecuted for the offence.

30. The wide general principle which underlies the defence of privilege is the common convenience and welfare of society. The difference between absolute privilege and qualified privilege lies in the fact that whereas the one affords complete immunity the other can be destroyed by proof of malice on the part of the accused. This defence of absolute privilege and qualified privilege have been well settled that sort of privilege is dictated by public interests, but the welfare of society cannot leave the matter at that; it must have other occasions where a person can speak out his mind freely and without fear of any sort of action, although the statements made are defamatory in their nature.

31. Unlike civil law on the subject, the criminal law of defamation is a codified law and is contained in Sections 34 Spl.CC 461/2018 499 of IPC. For the offence of defamation who is the person aggrieved may be some time difficult to judge. Here in this case, allegations are made against the Complainant. Sec.198 of Cr.P.C., speaks initiation of procedure for filing of complaint on behalf of the person mentioned in the section. The proviso to Sec.198 of Cr.P.C., provides that some other person with the leave of the court concerned, can make a complaint on his or her behalf.

It is held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the first judgment that the said provision is valid in the eye of law. It is stated in the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Om Prakash Chautala Vs. Kanwar Bhan and others reported in (2014) 5 SCC 417 held as under:-

"It has been held that reputation is fundamentally a glorious amalgam and 77 Spl.CC 461/2018 unification of virtues which makes a man feel proud of his ancestry and satisfies him to bequeath it as a part of inheritance on posterity. It is nobility in itself for which a conscientious man would never barter it with all the tea of China or for that matter all the pearls of the sea. The said virtue has both horizontal and vertical qualities. When reputation is hurt, the man is half- dead. It is an honour which deserves to be equally preserved by the downtrodden and the privileged. The aroma of reputation is an excellence which cannot be allowed to be sullied with the passage of time. It is dear to life and on some occasions, it is dearer than life. And that is why it has become an inseparable facet of Article 21 of the Constitution. No one would 78 Spl.CC 461/2018 like to have his reputation dented and it is perceived as an honour rather than popularity."

114. Thus the reputation of a human being is fundamentally glorious amalgam and unification of virtues which makes a man feel proud of his ancestry. Learned counsel submitted that using of such words, as stated supra, has really hurt this Complainant and because of this allegation he is half-dead. The principles laid down in th aforesaid judgments relied upon by the counsel for the Complainant is aptly applies to the facts of the case.

115. As against this submission, counsel for the accused has placed reliance on the judgment of Hon'ble Gujarath High Court in Crl.Misc. Appln No.2546 of 2012 between Sudhir Agarwal Vs. State of Gujarath decided on 5.4.2018. But the facts of this case differs than the facts of the said judgment. Even in the course of the said judgment, Hon'ble Gujarath High Court observed relying upon the judgment of Supreme Court in the case of Ramanbhai 79 Spl.CC 461/2018 Nagjibhai Patel Vs. Jaswantsingh Udesingh Dabhi and others reported in AIR 1968 SC 1162 as under:-

"We may state that the charge of bribery is in the nature of a criminal charge and has got to be proved beyond doubt. The standard of proof required is that of proving a criminal or a quasi
- criminal charge. A clear-cut evidence, wholly credible and reliable is required to prove the charge beyond doubt. Evidence merely probabilising and endeavouring to prove the fact on the basis of preponderance of probability is not sufficient to establish such a charge."

116. Here in this case also the allegations of bribary, corruption, cheating, influencing officers and getting the 80 Spl.CC 461/2018 land granted by influencing the Chief Minister and other authorities have been alleged by the accused. But these allegations are not proved by the accused.

117. When the counsel for the accused was advancing arguments, he has produced about 14 documents by filing list of documents dt.25.10.2019. These documents are not at all marked in evidence. He places reliance on the Karnataka Land Grant Rules, invitation card of the Complainant institution and other letters being addressed, so also copy of the complaint issued by the Dasanapura Panchayath issued under RTI Act etc. As these documents are not marked in evidence, they cannot be read in evidence. However, it is for the authorities concerned to take action for setting aside the grant, if at all there is any violation. The documents so produced are being obtained by the accused subsequent to filing of this complaint. Some documents are obtained by the accused during the pendency of this complaint. So, no evidentiary value can be attached to these documents. In this case, it is for the Complainant to establish the guilt of the accused 81 Spl.CC 461/2018 beyond all reasonable doubt. Sec.499 of Cr.P.C., speaks of definition of defamation.

118. Thus it is alleged that there is imputation of truth which public good requires to be made or published. But in this case though series of letters addressed, but there is no imputation of truth by the accused against the Complainant. Sec.499 of IPC does not place unreasonable restriction on the freedom of speech and expression and, hence, is not violative of Article 19(1)(a) of the Constitution. Therefore, this Section requires three essentials.

1) making or publishing any imputation concerning any person.

2) such imputation must have been made--

i) by words, either spoken or intended to be read; or

ii) by signs or

iii) by visible representations.

3) Such imputation must have been made with the intention of harming, or with knowledge or 82 Spl.CC 461/2018 having reason to believe that it will harm the reputation of the person concerning whom it is made.

119. Herein this case a complaint is filed by Complainant alleging defamation made against him by the accused, being a RTI activist and series of complaints have been filed but they have been rejected. Even the accused went to print and electronic media gave statement against the Complainant. Therefore, making known of defamatory matter after it has been written to some person other than the person of whom it is written, is publication in its legal sense. It is proved by the Complainant that to defame the complainant, this publication has been made and series of complaints have been addressed by the accused. A play which is woven out of the imagination of the author i.e., accused, can possibly contain more deadly imputations against the real persons than a mere narrative. Thus to say, this accused has woven out his own imagination about the allegations so made by him against the Complainant.

83 Spl.CC 461/2018

120. No doubt it has come in the evidence of the accused that there is no ill-will against the Complainant. But there is an imputation against the Complainant, although these allegations are made in the absence of actual ill-will, is not on that account to be accepted as being made bonafide. Conscious violation of law to another's prejudice is sufficient, though there may be no malice in fact. The defamatory words being used by the accused in various petitions/letters/complaints, etc., prima facie libellous and were used by the accused in his representations/ complaints etc.

121. The meaning which should be attached to 'harm' is not the ordinary sense in which the word is used.... By 'harm' is meant imputations on a man's character made and expressed to others, so as to lower him in their estimation and that anything which lowers him merely in his own estimation, certainly does not constitute defamation."

122. Thus the essence of offence of defamation is the harm caused to the reputation of a person. Character is 84 Spl.CC 461/2018 what a person actually is and reputation is what neighbours and others say he is. The abusive words used by the accused fulfills the ingredients of Sec.499 of IPC.

123. In Kartar Singh case reported in AIR 1956 SC 541, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India quoted with approval of the passage from the judgment of Cockburn, C.J., in Seymour Vs. Butterworth; reads thus:-

"Those who fill a public position must not be too thin skinned in reference to comments made upon them. It would often happen that observations would be made upon public men which they know from the bottom of their hearts were undeserved and unjust; yet they must bear with them and submit to be misunderstood for a time".

124. This principle also can be applied to the present facts of the case made out by the Complainant. Therefore, in the considered view of this court, the Complainant in this case is able to establish beyond all reasonable doubt 85 Spl.CC 461/2018 that the imputations in question stated above consists of words which are made in various petitions concerned the Complainant, emanated from the accused are made published and intended thereby to harm the reputation of the Complainant and hence the Complainant in this case is able to prove the point No.1 raised supra with legal evidence. Hence, I record my findings on the above point in the affirmative holding that the accused is found guilty of committing the offence under Sec.499 read with sect.500 of IPC.

125. Now the question comes with regard to the imposition of sentence. As this case is summons trial case, accused need not be heard on sentence.

126. So far as sentencing policy is concerned, this section says that whoever defames another shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years or with fine or with both.

127. Evidently, in this case accused is eking his livelihood as an LIC Agent and he is RTI Activist. There are 86 Spl.CC 461/2018 no mitigating circumstances so as to show any leniency in imposing sentence.

128. In considering the quantum of sentence in a case of defamation a number of factors, such as the type of defamation, the manner in which defamation was made, etc., will have to be taken into consideration. Accused being a RTI activist, wields a very powerful weapon in his hand, as an RTI activist, which can mould the public opinion very easily. Hence, the accused is required to attach more care and caution in publishing or while making allegations by writing applications / lodging complaints, etc., which are likely to harm the reputation and good name of others. It is common knowledge that publishing scandalous articles sometimes get wide publicity and the circulation increases and consequently the income of the journalists also increases. This, therefore calls for a deterrent punishment and a mere sentence of fine in such cases will not at all adequate. For such person to pay the fine is very easy and it would not deter him from publishing again one equally libellous article or submitting 87 Spl.CC 461/2018 representation before various authorities. The accused has not justified in submitting such representations without ascertaining the truthfulness of the same. It has come in the evidence of the PW1 - Complainant that accused demanded Rs.2 lakhs from him and otherwise he threatened to him that he will publish in the news papers or he will fight before respective authorities alleging illegality etc. Thus where the accused has acted in a reckless way and without due care and caution and without making any attempt to find veracity of facts before publishing such representations before various authorities, impugned articles, representations etc., in the considered view of this court a sentence of six months of simple imprisonment and a fine of Rs.25,000/- if levied against the accused would meet the ends of justice. Accordingly, I record my findings on the above point No.1 in the affirmative.

129. Point No.2:- As a result of my foregoing discussion and reasons stated thereon, accused is found guilty of offence under punishable U/s. 499 r/w Sec.500 of 88 Spl.CC 461/2018 IPC. Accordingly, acting under Sec.255(2) of Cr.P.C., I proceed to pass the following:-

ORDER Accused is found guilty of offence punishable U/s. 499 r/w 500 of IPC.
Accused is sentenced to undergo S.I. for a period of six months and also to pay a fine of Rs.25,000/-. In default of payment of fine amount, accused is further sentenced to undergo S.I. for two months.
Out of the fine amount, Rs.20,000/- be paid as compensation to the Complainant as per Sec.357 of Cr.P.C. and remaining Rs.5000/- be deposited to the State.
Bail bond of the accused and his surety stands cancelled.

So far as defamation is concerned, as a principle
of equity, every man is entitled to have his reputation
preserved intact. A man's reputation is his property and
possibly more valuable than other properties, and any
words calculated to infringe this right affords a good cause
of action.
It is stated that "no man may disparage or
destroy the reputation of another. Every man has a right to
have his good name maintained unimpaired. This right is a
jus in rem, a right absolute and good against all the world.
Then what is defamation? From what has been
stated above the question of defamation has been primary
Spl.CC 461/2018
linked up with one's reputation that one commands among
one's fellow beings and it is the infringement of this right
to have one's reputation preserved intact that gives the
cause of action. Broadly speaking defamation may be
defined as a false and damaging statement. Salmond has
defined it as a wrong that consists in the publication of a
false and defamatory statement respecting another without
lawful justification. It is conventional to say that,
defamation includes a statement concerning any person
which exposes him to hatred, ridicule or contempt. But this
statement is no longer considered as exhaustive. The best
method of approach to the definition of defamation is to
consider it from the point view of the right which the
defamatory statement is alleged to infringe. No doubt
one's reputation includes all the moral and material
advantages to which it may entitle him in his relationship
with the Society as a whole. One's reputation may be so
well established that nothing said or done on the part of
the accused could harm it but still the accused would be
liable not because he had harmed the plaintiff's reputation
Spl.CC 461/2018
but for his deprived intention and his tendency to cause
harm.
As could be seen from the allegations made in
the complaint and documentary evidence adduced by the
Complainant, it is specifically alleged by the Complainant
that this accused has used abusive language, the utterance
of abusive and insulting language though can be regarded
as penal both as an offence against society in general and
as tending to provoke a breach of peace, yet for the
purposes of enforcing a civil liability for defamation the use
of the abuse or vulgar language addressed merely to cause
mental pain to the person addressed may not afford any
ground for such a claim unless its effect is to hurt his
reputation or to expose him to hatred, contempt, ridicule,
or obloquy, or to make him to be shunned or avoided by
those who otherwise have associated with him.
Certain tests have to be conducted whether
such a statement did by the accused are really defamatory
in nature or not. That a certain statement is defamatory is
to be adjudged from the point of view of ordinary, just and
Spl.CC 461/2018
reasonable people. The person to whom the statement is
published may be one of the class of those persons who
always attach a sinister meaning to every word that is
uttered. Here in this case, series of letters / allegations
have been addressed by the accused person, as per the
case of the complainant before various authorities alleging
that he has committed cheating, fraud, created false
documents, illegally occupied the landed property of the

The reading of Section will reveal that the
offence of defamation for which Sec.499 of IPC makes a
provision, is presented here in a form materially at
variance on two important points from that in which the
offence is understood in English law. Even the very
principle underlying the two forms of offence is different.
So far as, application of this definition in India in the
Spl.CC 461/2018
matter of proceedings of defamation, there distinction
maintained between the criminal proceedings and civil
proceedings for defamation. So far as criminal proceedings
are concerned, the law of defamation is not matter of
common law, but is matter of statute and of Sec.499 of IPC.
In a case of present nature, heavy burden lies on
the accused to prove his defence of justification or truth. In
criminal cases however truth of the statements alleged to
be defamatory is only a defence when the truth has come
out for public good. In India, this law is enacted In Indian
Penal Code . Exception 1 to Sec.499 of the Indian Penal
Code is culled out above says it is not defamation to impute
anything which is true concerning any person, if it be for
public good that the imputation should be made or
published. Whether or not it is for the public good is a
question of fact.

the person of whom it is written, is publication in its legal
sense. It is proved by the Complainant that to defame the
complainant, this publication has been made and series of
complaints have been addressed by the accused. A play
which is woven out of the imagination of the author i.e.,
accused, can possibly contain more deadly imputations
against the real persons than a mere narrative. Thus to say,
this accused has woven out his own imagination about the
allegations so made by him against the Complainant.
No doubt it has come in the evidence of the
accused that there is no ill-will against the Complainant.
But there is an imputation against the Complainant,
although these allegations are made in the absence of
actual ill-will, is not on that account to be accepted as
being made bonafide. Conscious violation of law to
another's prejudice is sufficient, though there may be no
malice in fact. The defamatory words being used by the
accused in various petitions/letters/complaints, etc., prima
facie libellous and were used by the accused in his
representations/ complaints etc.
In considering the quantum of sentence in a
case of defamation a number of factors, such as the type of
defamation, the manner in which defamation was made,
etc., will have to be taken into consideration. Accused
being a RTI activist, wields a very powerful weapon in his
hand, as an RTI activist, which can mould the public
opinion very easily. Hence, the accused is required to
attach more care and caution in publishing or while making
allegations by writing applications / lodging complaints,
etc., which are likely to harm the reputation and good
name of others. It is common knowledge that publishing
scandalous articles sometimes get wide publicity and the
circulation increases and consequently the income of the
journalists also increases. This, therefore calls for a
deterrent punishment and a mere sentence of fine in such
cases will not at all adequate. For such person to pay the
fine is very easy and it would not deter him from publishing
again one equally libellous article or submitting
Spl.CC 461/2018
representation before various authorities. The accused
has not justified in submitting such representations without
ascertaining the truthfulness of the same. It has come in
the evidence of the PW1 - Complainant that accused
demanded Rs.2 lakhs from him and otherwise he
threatened to him that he will publish in the news papers
or he will fight before respective authorities alleging
illegality etc. Thus where the accused has acted in a
reckless way and without due care and caution and without
making any attempt to find veracity of facts before
publishing such representations before various authorities,
impugned articles, representations etc., in the considered
view of this court a sentence of six months of simple
imprisonment and a fine of Rs.25,000/- if levied against the
accused would meet the ends of justice. Accordingly, I
record my findings on the above point No.1 in the
affirmative.
conclusion:
Spl.CC 461/2018

"It has been held that reputation is
fundamentally a glorious amalgam and
Spl.CC 461/2018
unification of virtues which makes a
man feel proud of his ancestry and
satisfies him to bequeath it as a part of
inheritance on posterity. It is nobility in
itself for which a conscientious man
would never barter it with all the tea of
China or for that matter all the pearls
of the sea. The said virtue has both
horizontal and vertical qualities. When
reputation is hurt, the man is half-
dead. It is an honour which deserves to
be equally preserved by the
downtrodden and the privileged. The
aroma of reputation is an excellence
which cannot be allowed to be sullied
with the passage of time. It is dear to
life and on some occasions, it is dearer
than life. And that is why it has
become an inseparable facet of Article
of the Constitution. No one would
Spl.CC 461/2018
like to have his reputation dented and
it is perceived as an honour rather
than popularity."
1) making or publishing any imputation
concerning any person.
2) such imputation must have been made--
ii) by signs or
iii) by visible representations.
3) Such imputation must have been made with
the intention of harming, or with knowledge or
Spl.CC 461/2018
having reason to believe that it will harm the
reputation of the person concerning whom it is
made.
Spl.CC 461/2018
The meaning which should be attached to 'harm'
is not the ordinary sense in which the word is used.... By
'harm' is meant imputations on a man's character made
and expressed to others, so as to lower him in their
estimation and that anything which lowers him merely in
his own estimation, certainly does not constitute
defamation."
Thus the essence of offence of defamation is the
harm caused to the reputation of a person. Character is
Spl.CC 461/2018
what a person actually is and reputation is what
neighbours and others say he is. The abusive words used
by the accused fulfills the ingredients of Sec.499 of IPC.
This principle also can be applied to the present
facts of the case made out by the Complainant. Therefore,
in the considered view of this court, the Complainant in
this case is able to establish beyond all reasonable doubt
Spl.CC 461/2018
that the imputations in question stated above consists of
words which are made in various petitions concerned the
Complainant, emanated from the accused are made
published and intended thereby to harm the reputation of
the Complainant and hence the Complainant in this case is
able to prove the point No.1 raised supra with legal
evidence. Hence, I record my findings on the above point in
the affirmative holding that the accused is found guilty of
committing the offence under Sec.499 read with sect.500
of IPC .
Now the question comes with regard to the
imposition of sentence. As this case is summons trial case,
accused need not be heard on sentence.
So far as sentencing policy is concerned, this
section says that whoever defames another shall be
punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may
extend to two years or with fine or with both.
Evidently, in this case accused is eking his
livelihood as an LIC Agent and he is RTI Activist. There are
Spl.CC 461/2018

imposing sentence.

case_summary: The complainant, Sanjay Chiripal, alleged defamation against the accused, G.S. Saini and Tilak Raj Kapoor, based on a letter dated 29.07.2012, which contained allegedly defamatory statements and was sent to the Lieutenant Governor and various authorities. Although the letter didn't directly name Chiripal, he argued that it clearly referred to him, harming his reputation. He contended that the letter falsely labeled him as a "habitual complainant" who harassed society members and government officials. The complainant claimed the statements were made with malicious intent and were not covered by any exceptions under Section 499 of the IPC. Defamation under Section 499 IPC requires intentional harm or knowledge that the statements could harm the person’s reputation.
case_decision: The court ruled that although some portions of the letter were unfavorably worded, they did not amount to defamation. The court noted that the letter primarily targeted the Assistant Registrar of Cooperative Societies and addressed broader issues of mismanagement within the society. Any mention of Chiripal was incidental and aimed at highlighting existing disputes, not defaming him. Given the longstanding litigation history between the parties, the court found no malice or intention to defame. Thus, the accused were acquitted of the charges under Sections 499/500 read with Section 34 of the IPC.
