Hosapete Abubakar vs M A Kasim Musliyar on 12 April, 2023

Author: P.N.Desai

Bench: P.N.Desai

                                                  -1-
                                                          CRL.A No. 1265 of 2012




                           IN THE HIGH COURT OF KARNATAKA AT BENGALURU

                               DATED THIS THE 12TH DAY OF APRIL, 2023

                                                 BEFORE
                                 THE HON'BLE MR JUSTICE P.N.DESAI

                                 CRIMINAL APPEAL NO.1265 OF 2012

                      BETWEEN:

                           HOSAPETE ABUBAKAR
                           AGED ABOUT 65 YEARS
                           S/O. MOHAMMED
                           DERLAKATTE,
                           MANGALORE.
                                                                    ...APPELLANT
                      (BY SRI ISMAIL MUNEEB MUSBA, ADVOCATE)

                      AND:

                      1.    M.A. KASIM MUSLIYAR
                            AGED ABOUT 60 YEARS
                            S/O. ABDUL REHMAN MUSLIYAR
                            R/O. ANSAR MANZIL
                            POST MUGRAL
Digitally signed by         KASARGOD DISTRICT.
NAGARATHNA M
Location: HIGH
COURT OF              2.    B.K. ABDUL KADER MUSLIYAR
KARNATAKA
                            AGED ABOUT 45 YEARS
                            S/O. MOHAMMED HAJI
                            R/O. BEDRAKAD HOUSE
                            KODUNGAL, BANTWAL TALUK
                            WORKING AT BUMBRAN JUMA MASJID
                            POST KUMBRAN, KUMBLE
                            KASARGOD.
                                                                 ...RESPONDENTS

                      (BY SRI SHRAVAN BHARADVAJ, ADVOCATE
                          FOR SRI B.S. SACHIN, ADVOCATE)
                              -2-
                                      CRL.A No. 1265 of 2012




     THIS CRL.A. IS FILED U/S.378(4) CR.P.C  BY THE
ADVOCATE FOR THE APPELLANT PRAYING TO SET ASIDE THE
ORDER OF ACQUITTAL DATED 13.09.2012 PASSED BY THE
JMFC. (III COURT), MANGALORE, IN C.C. NO.1047/2008 -
ACQUITTING THE RESPONDENT/ACCUSED FOR THE OFFENCE
PUNISHABLE UNDER SECTION 500 AND 501 OF IPC.

     THIS APPEAL COMING ON FOR FURTHER DICTATION,
THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:

                        JUDGMENT

This appeal arises out of judgment of acquittal passed by JMFC (III Court), Mangalore, D.K., dated 13.09.2012 in C.C.No.1047/2008, wherein the learned JMFC acquitted accused Nos.1 and 2 for the offences punishable under Sections 500 and 501 of Indian Penal Code (for short hereinafter referred to as 'IPC').

2. In brief the case of the prosecution is that the appellant/complainant is a respectable person and is a philanthropist and a social worker. The appellant was also the President of Derlakatte Mosque Trust. It is further contended that knowing fully well regarding the position and status of the complainant, the accused persons got published defamatory articles against the complainant in -3- CRL.A No. 1265 of 2012 'Jaya Kiran' newspaper at page No.3 on 13.05.2006 stating that the complainant has tortured his own father and also attempted to murder his own father. It is contended that by this imputation, the complainant was defamed in the society. In this regard, the complainant issued legal notice to the editor, printer and publisher of the newspaper regarding the defamatory articles published by them and later a case was registered against printer and publisher of the said newspaper in C.C.No.3878/2006. Thereafter the printer and publisher of said newspaper appeared before the court and filed a memo stating that the said imputations were made by the Musliyars i.e., the accused in this case. Then the publisher and printer of Jaya Kiran newspaper published another publication on 07.08.2007 under the caption "Hosapete Abubakkaaravara Hesaru Kedisuva Shadyantra" and expressed their regret for having edited, printed and published the said defamatory imputation supplied by the said musliyars. The complainant accepted the regret of the editor, printer and publisher and subsequently sought permission to withdraw -4- CRL.A No. 1265 of 2012 the complaint filed against the printer, publisher and editor of Jaya Kiran newspaper. Subsequently, when the complainant came to know that it was the accused who gave the malicious imputations in the newspaper against the appellant, filed a private complaint under Section 200 of Code of Criminal Procedure (for short hereinafter referred to as 'Cr.P.C.') for the offence under Sections 500 and 501 of IPC against them.

3. Thereafter, he got himself as PW.1 and four more witnesses have been examined as PWs.2 to 5 and got marked sixteen documents as Exs.P1 to P16. After completing the trial and hearing the arguments, learned JMFC acquitted the accused and hence, the complainant has challenged the said acquittal in this appeal.

4. Heard Sri. Ismail Muneeb Musba, learned counsel appearing for the appellant and Sri. Shravan Bharadavaj for Sri. B.S.Sachin, learned counsel appearing for the respondents.

-5-

CRL.A No. 1265 of 2012

5. Learned counsel for the appellant argued that judgment of acquittal passed by the Trial Court is contrary to the law, facts and evidence on record. The Trial Court has failed to formulate proper points for consideration and has erroneously acquitted the accused and the same is not just and proper. The publication of the said article in 'Jaya Kiran' newspaper has drastically affected the image of the appellant in the eyes of common man in the society. The imputation has been made with an intention to harm the reputation of the appellant and knowing fully well that such publication will damage the reputation of the appellant. Further that the intention by the accused to cause harm is the most essential 'sina qua non' of the offence under Section 499 of IPC.

6. Learned counsel for the appellant argued that the malicious imputation published covers all the basic ingredients of defamation as the statement published was totally false. The Trial Court failed to consider the motive by the accused in making the malicious imputation against -6- CRL.A No. 1265 of 2012 the appellant. The Trial Court has failed to realize the mental trauma and agony undergone by the appellant. The learned JMFC ought to have placed reliance on the evidence of PWs.2 and 3, former reporter and editor of the Jaya Kirana, Kannada newspaper who have stated that two accused came to the office along with one Ismail Shafti and it was on their request that article was published. The Trial Court has failed to scrutinize and appreciate the evidence on record by adopting the standards adopted by the judicial forums. On the other hand, the Trial Court without considering the effect of cross-examination straight way proceeded to accept the evidence in examination-in-chief, without proper scrutiny. Learned JMFC failed to realize that the evidence of the prosecution witnesses discloses that it is the accused persons who requested the PWs.2 and 3, former reporter and editor to publish the said article. The learned counsel argued that the Trial Court has failed in applying the principles propounded in Exception 4 stated to the Section 499 of IPC. The said imputation harmed the reputation of -7- CRL.A No. 1265 of 2012 the appellant. The learned counsel argued that the complainant has also examined two independent witnesses about reputation of the complainant and damage to his reputation. The Trial Court without appreciating the same and without considering the oral and documentary evidence, and without properly appreciating the materials on record has wrongly acquitted the accused. On the other hand, the complainant by his own evidence and examining two more witnesses on his behalf and documentary evidence has proved the ingredients of the offence under Sections 499 and 501 of IPC. Therefore, as there is no proper appreciation of evidence, the judgment of acquittal being erroneous has resulted in miscarriage of justice. Learned counsel for the appellant in support of his contention relied on the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Mohd. Abdulla Khan Vs. Prakash K reported in (2018) 1 SCC 615 wherein at paragraph No.22 the Hon'ble Supreme Court held as under:

"22. K.M.Mathew Vs. K.A.Abraham, (2002) 6 SCC 670 has nothing to do with the question -8- CRL.A No. 1265 of 2012 of vicarious liability. The argument in K.M. Mathew case was that in view of Section 7 of the Press and Registration of Books Act, 1867 only the Editor of a newspaper could be prosecuted for defamation. Such a submission was rejected holding that Section 7 does not create any immunity in favour of persons other than the Editor of a newspaper. It only creates a reubttable presumption that the persons whose name is shown as the Editor of the newspaper is responsible for the choice and publication of the material in the newspaper. K.M. Mathew case made it clear that if a complaint contains allegations (which if proved would constitute defamation), person other than the one who is declared to be the editor of the newspapers can be prosecuted if they are alleged to be responsible for the publication of such defamatory material."

7. He has also relied on the judgment of High Court of Bombay in the case of Muncherji Nusserwanji Cama Vs. The State of Maharashtra - Criminal Application No.97/2019 dated 18.11.2019 and he has referred to paragraph No.9 and the same reads as under: -9- CRL.A No. 1265 of 2012

"9. As far as liability is concerned, primarily a reporter is responsible for his act of defamation and vicarious responsibility is fastened only on the printer, publisher and editor of the newspaper, unless the contrary is proved. Having regard to the judicial pronouncements in this regard, it can safely be said that besides persons declared as editor, printer and publisher of a newspaper, only such persons could be prosecuted for an action of defamation against whom specific and clear allegations have been made in the complaint that either he was responsible for selection of the defamatory matter or had personal knowledge about the contents of the defamatory matter. In addition, it must also be averred in the complaint that such person had the intention to harm or had knowledge or reason to believe that the imputation will harm the reputation of the complainant. A perusal of the complaint filed by the respondent No.3 contains specific allegations against the applicants."

With these arguments, learned counsel prayed to set aside the judgment of acquittal.

- 10 -

CRL.A No. 1265 of 2012

8. Against this, learned counsel for the respondents argued that the Trial Court has rightly considered the evidence and has given reasons and held that there is nothing to show that the respondents/accused have given any such information. On the other hand, the evidence discloses that these accused are not knowing the printer, publisher or owner of the newspaper. The article itself does not indicate anything that these accused who have given the information to publish the same in the newspaper. Subsequently, editor, publisher and owner of the said paper have named these persons, only to escape their liability and somehow tried to close the case against them. There is no material to show that these accused have committed the offences as alleged. Learned counsel for the respondents argued that the judgment of acquittal is supported by reasons. Hence, he prayed to dismiss the appeal.

- 11 -

CRL.A No. 1265 of 2012

9. I have perused the appeal memorandum, impugned judgment of acquittal and also the evidence on record.

10. In order to attract the offence under Section 499 of the Indian Penal Code (for short 'the IPC') i.e., defamation firstly, the words must be defamatory; secondly, they must refer to the aggrieved party; thirdly, they must be maliciously published. The section is having four explanations and ten exceptions. The explanation amplify the scope of the section whereas the exceptions take out certain things out of application of the section. In order to constitute an offence of defamation, the essential ingredient is to make an imputation, concerning any person, with an intention to harm or with a knowledge or reason that such imputation will harm the reputation of such person. An imputation without an intention to harm or without knowing or having reason to believe that it will harm the reputation of such person will not constitute an

- 12 -

CRL.A No. 1265 of 2012

offence of defamation. The punishment is prescribed under Section 500 of IPC.

11. It is relevant to state here that the complainant has alleged an offence under Section 501 of IPC. However, the said Section is not applicable to the accused/respondents. The accused are neither publishers nor editors or owner of newspaper. Therefore, what is required to be noticed is whether the alleged offence against the respondents in the evidence indicates an offence under Section 499 of IPC.

12. According to the evidence of PW.1, he knew very well that accused nos.1 and 2 i.e., the respondents were working as Musliyars in Kasargod Masjid and Umran Jumma Masjid of Kumble respectively. They were also collecting money for construction of Madarasa. He has also stated that there was misunderstanding between himself and the accused as he had advised them that collection of amount for construction of Madarasa was not proper. He has deposed that the accused persons for the said reason

- 13 -

CRL.A No. 1265 of 2012

got published an article in 'Jai Kiran' Kannada daily newspaper stating that the complainant tried to kill his father by running the Car over him and therefore, the villagers developed bad opinion about him and he was defamed. Hence, he had filed complaint against the printer and publisher of Jai Kiran newspaper. Since the printer and publisher gave explanation and regretted for the same, the complaint was withdrawn. However, the printer and publisher informed that it was published at the instance of the accused who are respondents in this appeal. Hence, he has lodged the complaint against present accused. His cross examination shows that accused no.2 is none other his sister's son. Both are known to him. He admits in the cross examination that he asked the accused to show the place of construction of Madarasa and they took him to the place and he has given Rs.5,00,000/- in the year 2004 for construction of Madarasa in Kumbra of Puttur Taluk. He has stated that Kumbra is a trust belonging to Karnataka Islamic Academy. He was the Vice President of Karnataka Islamic

- 14 -

CRL.A No. 1265 of 2012

Academy. Accused no.1 was the Secretary and accused no.2 was also the member of the said trust. There was some misunderstanding between himself and President of the said trust and he has also not attended the said trust activities for last 4 to 5 years. According to him he has given Rs.13,70,000/- to the President of the said trust. He has admitted that the accused persons are neither publisher nor editor of the newspaper. He has also admitted about filing of the case against the printer and the publisher of Jai Kiran newspaper and settlement of the matter. He has also admitted that he has lodged a complaint against these accused at Konaje Police Station and also lodged complaints at Bantwal and Ullal. He has also lodged a complaint against the accused in Musliyars Society at Kerala but he do not know whether police have filed 'B' report in this regard. He has stated that the accused in CC No.3878/2006 who are the printer and publisher in Jai Kiran newspaper have revealed the name of the accused/respondents herein, and hence, he has lodged the complaint.

- 15 -

CRL.A No. 1265 of 2012

13. After perusing the evidence, it is evident that that there is nothing in his evidence to show that with an intention to harm his reputation or impute at the instance of these accused article was published in the said 'Jai Kiran' newspaper. Merely because the article was published by somebody attributing certain utterness to any person and only at the say of this printer and publisher, the accused/respondents herein cannot be prosecuted unless it is shown that the said article was published concerning imputation at the instance of these respondents. It must be shown that such imputation was made directly or indirectly to lower moral or intellectual character of that person or lower the credit of that person. But nothing is stated by the complainant. On the other hand, they were known to each other, one of the accused is his relative and they were members of the trust. The accused are also religious teachers in their community. He has lodged a complaint against them to police and also at different places and therefore, the complainant is having ill will and enmity against the accused. His evidence requires

- 16 -

CRL.A No. 1265 of 2012

corroboration and it is not safe to base conviction only on his interested version.

14. I have perused the evidence of PW.2 - Reporter of Jai Kiran newspaper. He has deposed that in the year 2006, they had published the article against the complainant titled as 'Maulvigalibbarige Jeeva Bedarike' which is marked as Ex.P3. According to PW.2, the accused had come to their printing press with one Ismail Shafi and they have given information for publication of the said article. He has admitted that the printer and publisher have expressed their regret and the case was withdrawn against them. His cross examination shows that he does not know the whereabouts of the accused. He has no record to show that he was the printer or publisher of the said paper. He has not produced his licence. He does not know that Hospete Aboobakkar belongs to which place. He knew Ismail Shafi who brought the accused persons to the office. It is admitted that the article was published stating that it has came to the notice from public that complainant

- 17 -

CRL.A No. 1265 of 2012

tried to kill his father by running the Car over him. He has admitted that they will verify authenticity of the news before publishing any news. On what basis, he has published the said news is not forthcoming. There is absolutely nothing to show that the accused persons have requested him to publish the said article. It appears that just to escape the liability from the case filed against printer and publisher of Jai Kiran newspaper, they have simply named the accused persons without any basis.

15. PW.3 is the Editor of the said newspaper. He has also stated about the publication of the said news in the newspaper. According to him, the said news was given by one Ismail Shafi but the said person is not made as an accused in the present case. His cross examination also reveals that he has not verified the authenticity of the said news. He does not know the accused except Ismail Shafi. It is not mentioned that it was published at the instruction or information received from the accused. When he does not know the accused and the said Ismail Shafi who has

- 18 -

CRL.A No. 1265 of 2012

given information is not made a party, his evidence will not help to show that the accused persons were responsible for publication of the said article.

16. PW.4 and PW.5 are the witnesses to state about the reputation of the complainant. They do not have any information as to how this article was published. According to these two witnesses, the defamatory portion is that the complainant tried to kill his father.

17. I have also perused Ex.P3 - defamatory article. It is evident from the said article published in Jai Kiran newspaper that the accused persons have lodged a complaint to the Superintendent of Police, Kasargod regarding threatening of the accused persons by the complainant over phone and has hatched a criminal conspiracy. It is also stated in the newspaper that it was heard from the public that the complainant earlier tried to kill his father by running the Car over him. Therefore, on perusing the said defamatory article what can be said is that the complainant tried to kill his father according to

- 19 -

CRL.A No. 1265 of 2012

the publication and the same was heard from the public whereas the accused have not informed the PW2 or PW3 that the complainant tried to kill his father. On the other hand, it is also evident that the complainant has lodged the complaint against the accused persons at different places and moreover they are relatives and there is ill will between them. Therefore, the evidence of the complainant and his witnesses does not show that the accused were responsible for publication of the said article. There is no basis for publication of the said article by the publisher and printer of the said newspaper. Now, it appears just to escape the punishment for defamation, the printer and publisher of Jai Kiran newspaper have blamed the accused. When either the printer or publisher of the newspaper does not know whereabouts of the accused persons, on what basis they had published the said article is not forthcoming. They knew only about one Ismail Shafi whereas he is not the accused in the present case. The accused persons have not given any written letter, article or material for publication in the said newspaper and there

- 20 -

CRL.A No. 1265 of 2012

is nothing to show that the said article was published at the instance of the accused. Absolutely, there is no basis to show that the accused persons have supplied any information and/or given information or at their behest, this article was published. Merely because the printer and publisher names the accused, they cannot be held responsible unless there is any evidence to show that the said article was published at the instance of the accused with an intention to harm the reputation of the complainant or lower his reputation in the eyes of public. Merely because some article is published against the complainant, the accused cannot be held liable for the same. It is the printer and publishers who were responsible for publication of the article. However, the complainant has withdrawn the case against them and at their instance, the complainant has lodged the complaint against present accused. There is nothing to show that the accused with an intention tried to harm or lower the reputation of the complainant.

- 21 -

CRL.A No. 1265 of 2012

18. The entire evidence of the complainant would clearly show that there is no legally admissible evidence to show that the accused are responsible for publication of the said article against the complainant. The main allegation that the complainant tried to kill his father was published in the newspaper as it was heard from general public whereas the said information was not received from the accused persons. Absolutely, there is no ground to show that the accused have committed the offence as alleged.

19. The learned Judge of trial court after considering the entire evidence on record has come to the conclusion that the complainant/appellant has failed to prove the guilt and the evidence of the complainant creates a doubt. Hence trial court has given benefit of doubt. to the accused and acquitted them.

20. The decision relied on by the learned counsel for the appellant of High Court of Judicature at Bombay in Muncherji Nusserwanji Cama & Another vs. The

- 22 -

CRL.A No. 1265 of 2012

State of Maharashtra & Another in Criminal Application No.97/2019 (DD 18.11.2019) will not help the appellant as there is no dispute about the proposition laid down therein. On the other hand, if paragraph 9 of the judgment is perused, then the said judgment will not help the complainant. In order to attract the offence under Section
of the Indian Penal Code (for short 'the IPC ') i.e.,
defamation firstly, the words must be defamatory;
secondly, they must refer to the aggrieved party; thirdly,
they must be maliciously published. The section is having
four explanations and ten exceptions. The explanation
amplify the scope of the section whereas the exceptions
take out certain things out of application of the section. In
order to constitute an offence of defamation, the essential
ingredient is to make an imputation, concerning any
person, with an intention to harm or with a knowledge or
reason that such imputation will harm the reputation of
such person. An imputation without an intention to harm
or without knowing or having reason to believe that it will
harm the reputation of such person will not constitute an
offence of defamation. The punishment is prescribed
under Section 500 of IPC.

case_summary: In the case Ayub H.H vs. State of Kerala, the Kerala High Court addressed a criminal revision petition concerning a defamation complaint filed against the petitioner. The petitioner claimed that a Facebook post by the respondent contained defamatory statements damaging to his reputation and business. The post alleged misconduct related to the petitioner's firm, prompting the petitioner to file a complaint under Sections 500, 501, and 502 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC). The Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate dismissed the complaint, concluding there was insufficient evidence to show that the respondent intended to harm the petitioner's reputation.
case_decision: The Kerala High Court upheld the dismissal of the complaint, stating that criticism of a product or service does not constitute defamation. The court emphasized that under Section 499 IPC, defamation requires an intention to harm or knowledge that harm would result from the statements made. The court found that the statements in the Facebook post were criticisms of the petitioner’s product rather than personal attacks, thus falling outside the purview of defamation. The court referenced precedent that clarified the legal interpretation of defamation, concluding that the petitioner’s claim lacked sufficient grounds for proceeding further. Consequently, the revision petition was dismissed.

5. The counsel for the petitioner further argued that the 2nd respondent had caused damage to the brand of the petitioner and his business. The content of the Facebook post tarnished the reputation of the brand of the complainant and has adversely affected the sale of the product of the complainant's Firm.

6. The counsel for the petitioner further argued that the Magistrate committed an error in relying on the dictum in 2018 KHC 160. The content in the body of Section 499 IPC is regarding the harm to the reputation of any person, which necessarily means that the Section deals with individuals. The reasoning of the Magistrate is unsustainable.

7. I have heard the learned counsel for the petitioner, the learned Public Prosecutor representing the 1 st respondent and the learned counsel appearing for the 2 nd respondent. I have also perused the certified copies of the depositions of PWs 1 to 4 made available by the counsel for Crl.R.P. No.266/2023 :5: the petitioner.

8. The statements of the witnesses would show that the content of the Facebook post is regarding the product of the Firm of the petitioner. The 2 nd respondent has criticised the product. Criticism of any product/service made by a citizen cannot be treated as defamatory though such criticism may not be of the liking of the manufacturers/producers.

9. Section 499 IPC defines defamation as "Whoever, by words either spoken or intended to be read, or by signs or by visible representations, makes or publishes any imputation concerning any person intending to harm, or knowing or having reason to believe that such imputation will harm, the reputation of such person, is said, except in the cases hereinafter excepted, to defame that person. This Court in the judgment in Malayala Manorama Company Limited and others v. Deepak J. M. and others [2018 KHC 160] has held that what is the content in the body of Section 499 IPC is regarding the harm to the reputation of any person. Any criticism or loss of reputation of any product Crl.R.P. No.266/2023 :6: therefore cannot be treated as defamatory.

In the afore circumstances, I do not find any reason to interfere with the order dated 19.12.2022 of the Court of Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Ernakulam in CMP No.760/2022. The Criminal Revision Petition is therefore dismissed.

Sd/-

N. NAGARESH, JUDGE aks/17.10.2023

case_summary: In the case of Thimmappa Bhat vs. Rama Naika J, the Karnataka High Court reviewed a Criminal Petition seeking to quash an order from the Additional Senior Civil Judge and JMFC, Puttur, which had taken cognizance of a complaint for defamation under Sections 499 and 500 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC). The respondent, Rama Naika, alleged that the petitioner, Thimmappa Bhat, published defamatory remarks about him in the Vijayavani Kannada newspaper. These remarks accused the respondent of misappropriating funds from a school and issuing illegal transfer certificates to students, which purportedly harmed the respondent's reputation. The petitioner contended that the publication was made in good faith and stemmed from a departmental inquiry that resulted in a penalty against the respondent, indicating the comments were based on the respondent’s conduct as a public servant. The complaint was dismissed by the learned Magistrate, leading to the current petition.
case_decision: Justice Hemant Chandangoudar determined that the remarks made by the petitioner were related to the respondent's performance in his public role and fell under the second exception of Section 499 IPC, which protects good faith expressions concerning a public servant's conduct. The court noted that to establish an offense of defamation, there must be an intention to cause harm through false statements, which was not evident in this case. Consequently, the High Court quashed the proceedings initiated against the petitioner, stating that continuing the complaint would constitute an abuse of the legal process, and allowed the petition.

                              ORDER

A private complaint under Section 200 of Cr.PC was filed by the respondent for the offences under Sections 499, 500 of IPC alleging that, the petitioner - accused had published certain derogatory remarks against the complainant in Vijayavani daily Kannada newspaper. The learned Magistrate took cognizance of the aforesaid offences. Taking exception to the same, this petition is filed.

2. The learned counsel for the petitioners submits that, the alleged derogatory remarks made against the complainant was published in good faith and in the absence of any intention to damage the reputation of the complainant, the impugned order passed by the learned Magistrate taking cognizance of the aforesaid offences is impermissible. He submits that, even accepting the derogatory remarks made against the complainant, on its face value, does not constitute the commission of the offences under Sections 499 and 500 of IPC. He further submits that in the absence of any damage caused to the complainant on account of derogatory remarks published, the complaint is not maintainable. In support, reliance is placed on the decision of the Co-ordinate Bench of this Court in the case of Mrs.Tara Ajai Singh vs. Mr.R.P.Sharma reported in ILR 2012 Kar 5619.

3. On the other hand, the learned counsel for the respondent-complainant submits that, the accused by making irresponsible imputation intentionally has damaged the reputation of the complainant. The learned Magistrate has -3- CRL.P No. 1518 of 2019 rightly taken cognizance of the aforesaid offences. In support, he places reliance on the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Mohd. Abdulla Khan vs. Prakash.K reported in (2018) 1 SCC 615.

4. I have examined the submissions made by the learned counsels for the parties.

5. A complaint was filed alleging that, the complainant had misappropriated the funds received by the school and also issued illegal transfer certificates to the students. Against the said allegation, a departmental enquiry was initiated. In the said departmental enquiry, the punishment was imposed by withholding one increment against the respondent, which is evident from document No.8 produced by the petitioner. It is clear that the alleged derogatory remark published against the complainant was in respect of his conduct in discharge of his public duties. The second exception to Section 499 of IPC specifies that it is not defamation to express in a good faith any opinion whatever respecting the conduct of a public servant in the discharge of his public functions.

6. The derogatory remarks alleged to have been published by the accused against the complainant falls under second exception to Section 499 of IPC. The coordinate Bench of this Court in the case of Tara Ajai Singh (supra) has held that to constitute an offence Under Section 499, there must be an intention to cause harm by making false statement without -4- CRL.P No. 1518 of 2019 lawful justification and the allegations must damage the person against whom the allegations are made.

7. In the absence of essential ingredients so as to constitute the offences under Sections 499, 500 of IPC, the cognizance taken by the learned Magistrate is impermissible and, the continuation of proceeding will be an abuse of process of law. Accordingly, I pass the following:

ORDER
i) Criminal petition is allowed.
ii) The impugned proceedings in CC No.312/2016 (PCR No.06/2015) on the file of the Additional Senior Civil Judge and JMFC, Puttur is hereby quashed.

Sd/-

case_summary: In The Phulchhab Daily News Paper vs. State of Gujarat, the petitioner, represented by its editor, sought to quash an order from the Judicial Magistrate that took cognizance of defamation charges under Sections 499, 500, 501, and 502 of the IPC. The complaint arose from news articles published in 1999, which allegedly defamed the complainant, a security guard and tenant, by accusing him and his son of abusing their status as members of the scheduled caste. The complaint was filed in 2004, over four years after the articles were published, raising issues of delay and lack of evidence. The petitioner argued that he was not the editor at the time of publication, and thus could not be held liable. The relevant legal provisions include Sections 467 and 468 of the Code of Criminal Procedure regarding the limitation period for filing complaints and Section 499 IPC concerning defamation.
case_decision: The Gujarat High Court ruled in favor of the petitioner, quashing the impugned order of the Judicial Magistrate. The court found that the complaint was filed beyond the statutory limitation period, thereby exceeding the magistrate's jurisdiction. It held that the proceedings constituted an abuse of process, as the petitioner could not be held liable for articles published prior to his editorship. The court emphasized that the complaint lacked sufficient evidence to support the allegations of defamation, leading to the conclusion that the summons issued against the petitioner were unjustified.

Also Known As Next Generation TV vs. The State Of Telangana, the petitioners, involved in the telecasting of a news program, sought to quash the proceedings of Criminal Case No.236 of 2018 for offenses under Sections 120-B (criminal conspiracy), 499 (defamation), 500 (punishment for defamation), and 502 (sale of printed or engraved substance containing defamatory matter) of the IPC. The complaint, filed by a businessman, alleged that a program aired on NTV defamed him by falsely branding him a "Mafia Don" involved in illegal activities related to banned gutkha products. The complainant claimed that these allegations damaged his reputation and sought an unconditional apology, which was not provided. The legal basis for the petitioners’ arguments rested on the assertion that the allegations did not constitute defamation and the cognizance taken by the Magistrate was unlawful due to lack of evidence linking them to the alleged offenses.
case_decision: The Telangana High Court allowed the petition of the first group of petitioners (A1, A3 to A5) and quashed the proceedings against them, stating that the complaint did not establish a prima facie case for defamation against these individuals. The court emphasized that mere association with a news organization does not entail criminal liability without specific allegations of individual involvement in the alleged defamatory acts. However, the petitions by A2 and A6 to A11 were dismissed, allowing proceedings to continue against them. The court ruled that the presence of A6 to A11 could be dispensed with during the trial, provided they filed an affidavit agreeing not to dispute the proceedings conducted on their behalf.

N.T.V. Also Known As Next Generation Tv vs The State Of Telangana on 7 February, 2023

           HON'BLE SRI JUSTICE K.SURENDER
 CRIMINAL PETITION Nos.11280, 11517 and 11536 OF 2022

COMMON ORDER:

1. Since the petitioners in all these petitions are seeking to quash the proceedings arising out of CC No.236 of 2018 on the file of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate at Hyderabad, they are being heard together and disposed by way of this Common Order.

2. Criminal Petition No.280 of 2022 is filed by the petitioners/A1, A3 to A5, Criminal Petition No.11517 of 2022 is filed by A2 and Criminal Petition No.11536 of 2022 is filed by A6 to A11in the calendar case.

3. The 2nd respondent filed a criminal complaint for the offence under Sections 120-B, 499, 500 & 502 of IPC against the petitioners. In the said complaint, it is stated that the complainant/2nd respondent herein is a successful businessman and runs charitable organizations. On 16.03.2018, a scrolling was repeatedly shown on NTV( next generation TV) regarding a person selling gutkha illegally, would be shown. Thereafter on the next day on 17.03.2018, a 2 program titled "Operation R.R.Gutka" was telecast on the A2/ NTV news channel, which was being run by A1company. The duration of the said program was more than 10 minutes which was repeatedly telecast. In the said news item it was shown that the complainant in the name of R.R.Gutka was selling poisonous substance which was banned. The news reader referred to and addressed complainant as 'Mafia Don', 'Kanthiri', 'Ketugaadu', 'Kachodi', Paniki malina Bachaagadu', 'Old city Don', 'K.D', 'Durmargudu', 'Adda Gadidha' and stated that he has amassed more than Rs.100 Crores at the cost of public health. The news reader, who is A6 reported that the complainant was running a Mafia Network in the Old City and was very influential. It was further mentioned that the complainant was associated with Dawood Ibrahim, a notorious terrorist. News item also mentioned that the complainant was a distributer of Goa Gutka and started manufacturing duplicate Goa Gutka and when he was confronted by Joshi, the owner and manager of 'Goa Gutka' the complainant had sought the help of Dawood Ibrahim, 3 who in turn threatened the said Joshi and ever since the complainant became 'Hameed Bhai'.

4. Further, the property of the sons of the complaint which was situated in Abids area was also shown on TV and mentioned that illegal activities were going on in the said complex. In the said broadcast, the complainant was branded as an associate of terrorist namely Dawood Ibrahim and mentioned that he was carrying out nefarious activities. Further, the complainant was addressed in the most vulgar and derogatory manner.

5. According to the complainant the said news item spread like wild fire and several persons enquired about the said news item. His reputation in the society had got down only on account of such news item being run on NTV-A2.

6. The complainant sent a legal notice on 19.03.2018 calling upon the petitioners/accused to issue unconditional apology. However, no apology was sought by the accused and neither apologized nor the conditions that were mentioned in the legal notice were addressed.

4

7. Learned Magistrate on the basis of the complaint has taken cognizance against the accused. The said order reads as follows:

"Perused the sworn statement and MOs 1 and 2. It is disclosed that the A2NTV has telecast a news item against complainant describing him as 'Mafia Don, Kantri, Ketugadu Addagadida, Durmargudu, KD, Old City don and described him as an Anti Social Eliment. In the news item it was alleged that the complaint was manufacturing a Gutka item and branding it as Goa Gutka and selling the same in the market and that when the owner of Goa Gutka by name Joshi questioned the complainant, ,he is alleged to have threatened the said Joshi by using the name of Dawood Ibrahim. The words and expressions used in the news bulletin are not warranted to convey the news to the public.
The material on record is constituting the prima facie case to attract an offence under Section 500 IPC.
Hence the cognizance of offence U/s.500 IPC is taken by exercising the power under Section 190(A) Cr.P.C against R1 to R11. Issue summons against them on payment of costs. Call on 12.06.2018."

8. Thereafter, aggrieved by taking cognizance against the petitioners, petitioners filed Revision Petition No.175 of 2018 before the Hon'ble Sessions Judge, which was also dismissed. Learned Sessions Judge found that the trial Court has rightly taken cognizance against the accused. The telecast of news branding the complainant as mafia don and using several abusive words amounts to offence of defamation. 5

9. Sri T.Pradyumna Kumar Reddy, learned Senior counsel appearing on behalf of Sri T.S.Anirudh Reddy, learned counsel for the petitioners would submit that the allegations made in the complaint do not make out any offence of defamation. Admittedly, the police had raided the premises of the complainant and during investigation it was found that the complainant was involved in manufacturing banned tobacco products. The cognizance taken by the learned Magistrate is bad in law and accordingly, the proceedings have to be quashed. In support of his contention, he relied on the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Managing Director, Castrol India Limited v. State of Karnataka and another [(2018) 17 Supreme Court Cases 275], wherein it is held as follows:

" 5. A reading of the complaint petition in question does not disclose that any specific act of the appellant resulted in commission of the offences alleged. In the compounding notice issued by the Inspector of Legal Metrology it has been mentioned that the allegedly offending goods (Castrol Plus) were manufactured plus packed by M/s. Castrol India Limited. The offence, therefore, has been committed by the Company and the appellant has been sought to be made vicariously liable merely because at the relevant point of time he was holding the office of Managing Director of Castrol India Limited."
6

10. He also relied upon the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of K.M.Mathew v. State of Kerala and another [(1992) 1 Supreme Court Cases 217], wherein it is held as follows:

"10. It is important to state that for a Magistrate to take cognizance of the offence as against the Chief Editor, there must be positive averments in the complaint of knowledge of the objectionable character of the matter. The complaint in the instant case does not contain any such allegation. In the absence of such allegation, the Magistrate was justified in directing that the complaint so far as it relates to the Chief Editor could not be proceeded with. To ask the Chief Editor to undergo the trial of the case merely on the ground of the issue of process would be oppressive. No person should be tried without a prima facie case. The view taken by the High Court is untenable. The appeal is accordingly allowed. The order of the High Court is set aside.°
11. In the case of P.Kiran v. State of Andhra Pradesh [2010 SCC OnLine AP 1267], this court held as follows:
"4. Thus Mens rea on the part of the accused is essential for defamation. In order to constitute Mens rea, the accused must have prior knowledge of commission of the offence. At this stage, it may be noted that A2 who is the Chief Reporter of Gemini Television at Visakhapatnam is not the petitioner herein and he is not seeking quashing of complaint insofar as he is concerned. The petitioner herein is A1 and he seeks quashing of the complaint insofar as he is concerned, under Section 482 Cr.P.C.
5. In Para 2 of the complaint it is stated that A1 is Managing Director of the Gemini Television and Teja News Electronic Media, Telecasting news throughout the State and also at the National level and that A2 is the Chief Reporter of Gemini Television at Visakhapatnam "responsible for gathering news and making news item from the Visakhapatnam District and causing its telecast through the Main station at Hyderabad." Thus even in the complaint, the complainant did not plead and allege that A1, as Managing Director had any role in gathering news or in making news items or in causing its telecast through the channel. No role is attributed to A1 by the complainant in telecasting the alleged 7 defamatory news item. When A1 had no role in affairs in Gemini Television, no vicarious liability on criminal side can be attributed to him unless there is any special or specific provision in Section 499 IPC mulcting him with such vicarious liability. It was held by this Court in Ravi Prakash v. J.C.Diwakar Reddy, 2010 (1) ALD (Crl.) 575 (AP), afer surveying case law in the subject including K.M.Mathew v. State of Kerala, AIR 1992 SC 2206, Dasari Narayana Rao v. R.D.Bhagvanas, 1986 Crl.LJ 888, by this Court, Prabhu Chawlaand v. A.U.Sheriff, 1995 Crl.LJ 1922, of the Karnataka High Court and S.Nihal Sigh v. Arjan Das, 1983 Crl. LJ 777, of the Delhi High Court."

12. In the case of Smt. Dipannita Jaiswal v. State of Assam and another, the Gauati High Court in Criminal Petition No.33 of 2015 held as follows:

"13. Chairman/Managing Director of a news channel can be held liable for publication of the offending news item only if it can be shown that he was somehow concerned with publication of the defamatory news item and that he had active knowledge thereof. As held in S Nihal Page No.# 5/7 Singh & Ors. V. Arjan Das; 1983 Cri. L.J. 777, an individual cannot be asked to answer the charge of defamation merely because he happened to be the Chairman of a company which owns a newspaper, without there being any further evidence as regards his participation in the actual management and administration of the affairs of the company.

14. So, the whole concept of fastening liability hinges on knowledge. As held in Kalanithi Maran v. A.Rathinaraj; 2017 SCC Online Mad 9723 and G K Mani v. New General Media Corporation (P.) Ltd; 2019 SCC Online Mad 8332, for fastening liability, what is of paramount importance is that knowledge has to be attributed to the accused person. In Kalanithi (supra), the petitioner is the Chairman-cum- MD of Sun TV Network Ltd. and the complaint was filed against him for telecasting an interview between the complainant and one person, on the allegation of falsity of the statement given in the news and consequently, the MD is equally responsible for telecasting such defamatory statement. The Hon'ble High Court held as below:-

"Vicarious liability under Press and Registration of Books Act, 1867, is not applicable to electronic media. Therefore, only general rule is applicable in the present case. To attract the offence of defamation, the imputation must have been made with the knowledge or 8 intention or at least with reason to believe that it will harm the person concerned."

13. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent/complainant submits that news item would not be telecast on its own unless there is consent of the management. The persons who are responsible for running the programme on the TV would be the Managing Directors and other Directors. The reporters are responsible for gathering news item and also news reader for making such comments. Further, the matter was scrolled on TV and in fact all the accused had knowledge about the said program, for which reason, the proceedings cannot be quashed.

14. Having perused the complaint, the grievance of the complainant is that he was shown as a criminal and also several words uttered, which are prima facie defamatory in nature. According to the complainant, news item was run on A2 channel and A6 was reporter/presenter of the program who made such abuses.

15. At para 17 of the complainant, it is mentioned that all the accused have telecast the program repeatedly without proof, making wild allegations resulting in scandalizing and 9 maligning the complaint's character in order to increase their viewer ratings. In the said circumstances, according to the complaint, all the accused have entered into criminal conspiracy for telecasting defamatory and derogatory news item in order to increase viewer ratings, as such all the accused are liable to be prosecuted under Section 120-B of IPC.

16. The complaint is made on an assumption that the management of A2, A3 to A5 who were managing the affairs of A1/M/s.Rachana Television Private Limited and also NTV/A2, were responsible for the defamatory content. Stating that on the basis of the program, the complainant's inference was that the management and the organization was also responsible and they have to be tried with the aid of Section 120-B of IPC for entering into criminal conspiracy to defame the complainant cannot be accepted. In the entire complaint, it is no where mentioned as to the role played by A1, A3 to A5. Only on the basis of general assumption that these persons are responsible, they are arrayed as accused. Admittedly hundreds of employees work to run the 24/7 10 news channel. Technical persons, reporters, producers, presenters and several other categories of employees are involved. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Managing Director, Castrol India Limited v. State of Karnataka (supra), while dealing with a case under Sections 39 and 74 of Standards of Weights and Measures Act, 1976 held that the Managing Director, though responsible for the conduct of the company business, cannot be mulcted with criminal liability unless specifically shown. Similar view was taken by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of K.M.Mathew's case. The proceedings against the Chief Editor were quashed on the ground that there was no allegation made in the complaint. Unless there is prima facie case, persons cannot be asked to undergo the rigmarole of a criminal trial.

17. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Pepsi Foods Limited Vs. Special Judicial Magistrate (2006) 7 SCC 296 at para-28 held that summoning of accused in a criminal case is a serious matter. Criminal law cannot be set into motion as a matter course. In Maksood Saiyed Vs. State of Gujarat (1980) 11 2 SCR 380=1980 (2) SCC 665 the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that merely holding an office in a company cannot be made basis to criminally prosecute holding them vicariously liable unless they are shown to be individually liable on the basis of material available.

18. The program was telecast on A2 channel/NTV. The said program was anchored by A6/news reporter/presenter. The other accused i.e., A7 is news editor, A8 to A11 are shown as news reporters. The reporters would be responsible for collecting news and news was presented by A6 and for the said reason of the content of the program being prima facie defamatory, the proceedings against A2, A6 to A11 cannot be quashed.

19. In the result, the proceedings against the petitioners/A1, A3 to A5 in C.C No.236 of 2018 on the file of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate at Hyderabad, are hereby quashed. Learned Senior Counsel alternatively argued that in the event of this Court not finding favour with the grounds, the attendance of the accused may be dispensed with. 12 Accordingly, the attendance of A6 to A11 is dispensed subject to the condition that the counsel proceeds with the trial in their absence and subject to filing an affidavit by the petitioners stating that in their absence the proceedings conducted by their counsel will not be disputed by them in any manner and also they shall not dispute their identity. However, the petitioners shall appear before the learned Magistrate as and when their presence is required. In the event of the petitioners' failure to appear when the Court directs, this order dispensing their attendance would stand cancelled. The 2nd Accused can be represented by any representative of the company in accordance with Section 305 of Cr.P.C.

20. Accordingly, Criminal Petition No.11280 of 2022 is allowed and Criminal Petition Nos.11517 and 11536 are dismissed. Consequently, miscellaneous petitions, if any, shall stand disposed.

the imputation must have been made with the knowledge or intention or at least with reason to believe that it will harm the
person concerned."
The complaint is made on an assumption that the
management of A2, A3 to A5 who were managing the affairs
of A1/M/s.Rachana Television Private Limited and also
NTV/A2, were responsible for the defamatory content. Stating

was that the management and the organization was also
responsible and they have to be tried with the aid of Section

A5. Only on the basis of general assumption that these

presenters and several other categories of employees are
involved. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of

Karnataka (supra), while dealing with a case under Sections

were quashed on the ground that there was no allegation

held that merely holding an office in a company cannot be
made basis to criminally prosecute holding them vicariously
liable unless they are shown to be individually liable on the
basis of material available.
The program was telecast on A2 channel/NTV. The said
program was anchored by A6/news reporter/presenter. The
other accused i.e., A7 is news editor, A8 to A11 are shown as
news reporters. The reporters would be responsible for
collecting news and news was presented by A6 and for the
said reason of the content of the program being prima facie
defamatory, the proceedings against A2, A6 to A11 cannot be

case_summary: In Swarna Roja vs. The State Of Telangana, multiple criminal petitions were consolidated to challenge the proceedings of Criminal Case No.236 of 2018, initiated against several petitioners for alleged defamation under Sections 120-B (criminal conspiracy), 499 (defamation), 500 (punishment for defamation), and 502 (sale of printed or engraved substance containing defamatory matter) of the IPC. The case arose from a news segment aired on NTV that accused the complainant, a businessman, of illegal activities related to gutkha sales, labeling him with derogatory terms and claiming ties to criminal elements, including the notorious figure Dawood Ibrahim. The complainant alleged that these broadcasts damaged his reputation, and he sent a legal notice demanding an apology, which was ignored. The Magistrate initially took cognizance of the complaint based on the evidence presented, stating it constituted a prima facie case of defamation.
case_decision: The Telangana High Court granted the petition of the first group of petitioners (A1, A3 to A5), quashing the proceedings against them, finding that the allegations did not establish a prima facie case for defamation. The court emphasized that merely being associated with the news organization does not imply liability without specific accusations of individual involvement in the defamatory acts. However, the petitions of A2 and A6 to A11 were dismissed, allowing proceedings to continue against them. The court held that the presence of A6 to A11 could be dispensed with during the trial, provided they filed an affidavit agreeing not to dispute the proceedings. The ruling reinforced the principle that all individuals cannot be held criminally liable without demonstrable involvement in the alleged defamatory conduct.

Swarna Roja vs The State Of Telangana on 7 February, 2023

           HON'BLE SRI JUSTICE K.SURENDER
 CRIMINAL PETITION Nos.11280, 11517 and 11536 OF 2022

COMMON ORDER:

1. Since the petitioners in all these petitions are seeking to quash the proceedings arising out of CC No.236 of 2018 on the file of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate at Hyderabad, they are being heard together and disposed by way of this Common Order.

2. Criminal Petition No.280 of 2022 is filed by the petitioners/A1, A3 to A5, Criminal Petition No.11517 of 2022 is filed by A2 and Criminal Petition No.11536 of 2022 is filed by A6 to A11in the calendar case.

3. The 2nd respondent filed a criminal complaint for the offence under Sections 120-B, 499, 500 & 502 of IPC against the petitioners. In the said complaint, it is stated that the complainant/2nd respondent herein is a successful businessman and runs charitable organizations. On 16.03.2018, a scrolling was repeatedly shown on NTV( next generation TV) regarding a person selling gutkha illegally, would be shown. Thereafter on the next day on 17.03.2018, a 2 program titled "Operation R.R.Gutka" was telecast on the A2/ NTV news channel, which was being run by A1company. The duration of the said program was more than 10 minutes which was repeatedly telecast. In the said news item it was shown that the complainant in the name of R.R.Gutka was selling poisonous substance which was banned. The news reader referred to and addressed complainant as 'Mafia Don', 'Kanthiri', 'Ketugaadu', 'Kachodi', Paniki malina Bachaagadu', 'Old city Don', 'K.D', 'Durmargudu', 'Adda Gadidha' and stated that he has amassed more than Rs.100 Crores at the cost of public health. The news reader, who is A6 reported that the complainant was running a Mafia Network in the Old City and was very influential. It was further mentioned that the complainant was associated with Dawood Ibrahim, a notorious terrorist. News item also mentioned that the complainant was a distributer of Goa Gutka and started manufacturing duplicate Goa Gutka and when he was confronted by Joshi, the owner and manager of 'Goa Gutka' the complainant had sought the help of Dawood Ibrahim, 3 who in turn threatened the said Joshi and ever since the complainant became 'Hameed Bhai'.

4. Further, the property of the sons of the complaint which was situated in Abids area was also shown on TV and mentioned that illegal activities were going on in the said complex. In the said broadcast, the complainant was branded as an associate of terrorist namely Dawood Ibrahim and mentioned that he was carrying out nefarious activities. Further, the complainant was addressed in the most vulgar and derogatory manner.

5. According to the complainant the said news item spread like wild fire and several persons enquired about the said news item. His reputation in the society had got down only on account of such news item being run on NTV-A2.

6. The complainant sent a legal notice on 19.03.2018 calling upon the petitioners/accused to issue unconditional apology. However, no apology was sought by the accused and neither apologized nor the conditions that were mentioned in the legal notice were addressed.

4

7. Learned Magistrate on the basis of the complaint has taken cognizance against the accused. The said order reads as follows:

"Perused the sworn statement and MOs 1 and 2. It is disclosed that the A2NTV has telecast a news item against complainant describing him as 'Mafia Don, Kantri, Ketugadu Addagadida, Durmargudu, KD, Old City don and described him as an Anti Social Eliment. In the news item it was alleged that the complaint was manufacturing a Gutka item and branding it as Goa Gutka and selling the same in the market and that when the owner of Goa Gutka by name Joshi questioned the complainant, ,he is alleged to have threatened the said Joshi by using the name of Dawood Ibrahim. The words and expressions used in the news bulletin are not warranted to convey the news to the public.
The material on record is constituting the prima facie case to attract an offence under Section 500 IPC.
Hence the cognizance of offence U/s.500 IPC is taken by exercising the power under Section 190(A) Cr.P.C against R1 to R11. Issue summons against them on payment of costs. Call on 12.06.2018."

8. Thereafter, aggrieved by taking cognizance against the petitioners, petitioners filed Revision Petition No.175 of 2018 before the Hon'ble Sessions Judge, which was also dismissed. Learned Sessions Judge found that the trial Court has rightly taken cognizance against the accused. The telecast of news branding the complainant as mafia don and using several abusive words amounts to offence of defamation. 5

9. Sri T.Pradyumna Kumar Reddy, learned Senior counsel appearing on behalf of Sri T.S.Anirudh Reddy, learned counsel for the petitioners would submit that the allegations made in the complaint do not make out any offence of defamation. Admittedly, the police had raided the premises of the complainant and during investigation it was found that the complainant was involved in manufacturing banned tobacco products. The cognizance taken by the learned Magistrate is bad in law and accordingly, the proceedings have to be quashed. In support of his contention, he relied on the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Managing Director, Castrol India Limited v. State of Karnataka and another [(2018) 17 Supreme Court Cases 275], wherein it is held as follows:

" 5. A reading of the complaint petition in question does not disclose that any specific act of the appellant resulted in commission of the offences alleged. In the compounding notice issued by the Inspector of Legal Metrology it has been mentioned that the allegedly offending goods (Castrol Plus) were manufactured plus packed by M/s. Castrol India Limited. The offence, therefore, has been committed by the Company and the appellant has been sought to be made vicariously liable merely because at the relevant point of time he was holding the office of Managing Director of Castrol India Limited."
6

10. He also relied upon the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of K.M.Mathew v. State of Kerala and another [(1992) 1 Supreme Court Cases 217], wherein it is held as follows:

"10. It is important to state that for a Magistrate to take cognizance of the offence as against the Chief Editor, there must be positive averments in the complaint of knowledge of the objectionable character of the matter. The complaint in the instant case does not contain any such allegation. In the absence of such allegation, the Magistrate was justified in directing that the complaint so far as it relates to the Chief Editor could not be proceeded with. To ask the Chief Editor to undergo the trial of the case merely on the ground of the issue of process would be oppressive. No person should be tried without a prima facie case. The view taken by the High Court is untenable. The appeal is accordingly allowed. The order of the High Court is set aside.°
11. In the case of P.Kiran v. State of Andhra Pradesh [2010 SCC OnLine AP 1267], this court held as follows:
"4. Thus Mens rea on the part of the accused is essential for defamation. In order to constitute Mens rea, the accused must have prior knowledge of commission of the offence. At this stage, it may be noted that A2 who is the Chief Reporter of Gemini Television at Visakhapatnam is not the petitioner herein and he is not seeking quashing of complaint insofar as he is concerned. The petitioner herein is A1 and he seeks quashing of the complaint insofar as he is concerned, under Section 482 Cr.P.C.
5. In Para 2 of the complaint it is stated that A1 is Managing Director of the Gemini Television and Teja News Electronic Media, Telecasting news throughout the State and also at the National level and that A2 is the Chief Reporter of Gemini Television at Visakhapatnam "responsible for gathering news and making news item from the Visakhapatnam District and causing its telecast through the Main station at Hyderabad." Thus even in the complaint, the complainant did not plead and allege that A1, as Managing Director had any role in gathering news or in making news items or in causing its telecast through the channel. No role is attributed to A1 by the complainant in telecasting the alleged 7 defamatory news item. When A1 had no role in affairs in Gemini Television, no vicarious liability on criminal side can be attributed to him unless there is any special or specific provision in Section 499 IPC mulcting him with such vicarious liability. It was held by this Court in Ravi Prakash v. J.C.Diwakar Reddy, 2010 (1) ALD (Crl.) 575 (AP), afer surveying case law in the subject including K.M.Mathew v. State of Kerala, AIR 1992 SC 2206, Dasari Narayana Rao v. R.D.Bhagvanas, 1986 Crl.LJ 888, by this Court, Prabhu Chawlaand v. A.U.Sheriff, 1995 Crl.LJ 1922, of the Karnataka High Court and S.Nihal Sigh v. Arjan Das, 1983 Crl. LJ 777, of the Delhi High Court."

12. In the case of Smt. Dipannita Jaiswal v. State of Assam and another, the Gauati High Court in Criminal Petition No.33 of 2015 held as follows:

"13. Chairman/Managing Director of a news channel can be held liable for publication of the offending news item only if it can be shown that he was somehow concerned with publication of the defamatory news item and that he had active knowledge thereof. As held in S Nihal Page No.# 5/7 Singh & Ors. V. Arjan Das; 1983 Cri. L.J. 777, an individual cannot be asked to answer the charge of defamation merely because he happened to be the Chairman of a company which owns a newspaper, without there being any further evidence as regards his participation in the actual management and administration of the affairs of the company.

14. So, the whole concept of fastening liability hinges on knowledge. As held in Kalanithi Maran v. A.Rathinaraj; 2017 SCC Online Mad 9723 and G K Mani v. New General Media Corporation (P.) Ltd; 2019 SCC Online Mad 8332, for fastening liability, what is of paramount importance is that knowledge has to be attributed to the accused person. In Kalanithi (supra), the petitioner is the Chairman-cum- MD of Sun TV Network Ltd. and the complaint was filed against him for telecasting an interview between the complainant and one person, on the allegation of falsity of the statement given in the news and consequently, the MD is equally responsible for telecasting such defamatory statement. The Hon'ble High Court held as below:-

"Vicarious liability under Press and Registration of Books Act, 1867, is not applicable to electronic media. Therefore, only general rule is applicable in the present case. To attract the offence of defamation, the imputation must have been made with the knowledge or 8 intention or at least with reason to believe that it will harm the person concerned."

13. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent/complainant submits that news item would not be telecast on its own unless there is consent of the management. The persons who are responsible for running the programme on the TV would be the Managing Directors and other Directors. The reporters are responsible for gathering news item and also news reader for making such comments. Further, the matter was scrolled on TV and in fact all the accused had knowledge about the said program, for which reason, the proceedings cannot be quashed.

14. Having perused the complaint, the grievance of the complainant is that he was shown as a criminal and also several words uttered, which are prima facie defamatory in nature. According to the complainant, news item was run on A2 channel and A6 was reporter/presenter of the program who made such abuses.

15. At para 17 of the complainant, it is mentioned that all the accused have telecast the program repeatedly without proof, making wild allegations resulting in scandalizing and 9 maligning the complaint's character in order to increase their viewer ratings. In the said circumstances, according to the complaint, all the accused have entered into criminal conspiracy for telecasting defamatory and derogatory news item in order to increase viewer ratings, as such all the accused are liable to be prosecuted under Section 120-B of IPC.

16. The complaint is made on an assumption that the management of A2, A3 to A5 who were managing the affairs of A1/M/s.Rachana Television Private Limited and also NTV/A2, were responsible for the defamatory content. Stating that on the basis of the program, the complainant's inference was that the management and the organization was also responsible and they have to be tried with the aid of Section 120-B of IPC for entering into criminal conspiracy to defame the complainant cannot be accepted. In the entire complaint, it is no where mentioned as to the role played by A1, A3 to A5. Only on the basis of general assumption that these persons are responsible, they are arrayed as accused. Admittedly hundreds of employees work to run the 24/7 10 news channel. Technical persons, reporters, producers, presenters and several other categories of employees are involved. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Managing Director, Castrol India Limited v. State of Karnataka (supra), while dealing with a case under Sections 39 and 74 of Standards of Weights and Measures Act, 1976 held that the Managing Director, though responsible for the conduct of the company business, cannot be mulcted with criminal liability unless specifically shown. Similar view was taken by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of K.M.Mathew's case. The proceedings against the Chief Editor were quashed on the ground that there was no allegation made in the complaint. Unless there is prima facie case, persons cannot be asked to undergo the rigmarole of a criminal trial.

17. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Pepsi Foods Limited Vs. Special Judicial Magistrate (2006) 7 SCC 296 at para-28 held that summoning of accused in a criminal case is a serious matter. Criminal law cannot be set into motion as a matter course. In Maksood Saiyed Vs. State of Gujarat (1980) 11 2 SCR 380=1980 (2) SCC 665 the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that merely holding an office in a company cannot be made basis to criminally prosecute holding them vicariously liable unless they are shown to be individually liable on the basis of material available.

18. The program was telecast on A2 channel/NTV. The said program was anchored by A6/news reporter/presenter. The other accused i.e., A7 is news editor, A8 to A11 are shown as news reporters. The reporters would be responsible for collecting news and news was presented by A6 and for the said reason of the content of the program being prima facie defamatory, the proceedings against A2, A6 to A11 cannot be quashed.

19. In the result, the proceedings against the petitioners/A1, A3 to A5 in C.C No.236 of 2018 on the file of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate at Hyderabad, are hereby quashed. Learned Senior Counsel alternatively argued that in the event of this Court not finding favour with the grounds, the attendance of the accused may be dispensed with. 12 Accordingly, the attendance of A6 to A11 is dispensed subject to the condition that the counsel proceeds with the trial in their absence and subject to filing an affidavit by the petitioners stating that in their absence the proceedings conducted by their counsel will not be disputed by them in any manner and also they shall not dispute their identity. However, the petitioners shall appear before the learned Magistrate as and when their presence is required. In the event of the petitioners' failure to appear when the Court directs, this order dispensing their attendance would stand cancelled. The 2nd Accused can be represented by any representative of the company in accordance with Section 305 of Cr.P.C.

20. Accordingly, Criminal Petition No.11280 of 2022 is allowed and Criminal Petition Nos.11517 and 11536 are dismissed. Consequently, miscellaneous petitions, if any, shall stand disposed.

case_summary: In the case of M/S. Rachana Television Private Limited vs. The State of Telangana, the Telangana High Court addressed multiple criminal petitions seeking to quash proceedings from Criminal Case No.236 of 2018 against the petitioners for alleged defamation under Sections 120-B (criminal conspiracy), 499 (defamation), 500 (punishment for defamation), and 502 (sale of printed or engraved substance containing defamatory matter) of the IPC. The complaint stemmed from a news segment broadcasted on NTV that accused the complainant, a businessman, of illegally selling banned gutkha products. The news portrayed him using derogatory terms and linked him to organized crime and a notorious terrorist, Dawood Ibrahim. Despite sending a legal notice demanding an apology, the accused failed to respond. The Magistrate took cognizance of the complaint, determining that the broadcast constituted a prima facie case of defamation.
case_decision: The High Court allowed the petitions of A1, A3 to A5, quashing the proceedings against them, as the allegations did not establish a prima facie case for defamation. The court emphasized that mere managerial status does not automatically implicate individuals without evidence of direct involvement in the alleged defamatory actions. However, the petitions from A2 and A6 to A11 were dismissed, allowing the proceedings to continue against them. The court maintained that the attendance of A6 to A11 could be dispensed with during the trial, provided they submitted an affidavit confirming their counsel's actions would not be contested. This ruling highlighted the necessity for specific allegations of individual liability in defamation cases, rather than assumptions based on corporate positions.

"10.
