Manraj Grewal vs State Of Haryana And Anr on 4 January, 2024

Author: Anoop Chitkara

Bench: Anoop Chitkara

                                                          Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:000277




CRM-M No. 39409 of 2018 (O&M)


                    IN THE HIGH COURT OF PUNJAB AND HARYANA
                                  AT CHANDIGARH

                                              CRM-M No. 39409 of 2018 (O&M)
                                              Reserved on: 16.10.2023.
                                              Pronounced on: 04.01.2024.


Manraj Grewal                                             .....Petitioner
                                    Versus

State of Haryana and another                              .....Respondents

CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE ANOOP CHITKARA

Present:      Mr. Manu K. Bhandari, Advocate
              for the petitioner.

              Mr. P.S. Poonia, Advocate, and
              Mr. Pulkit Dhanda, Advocate,
              for the respondents.

                        ****

ANOOP CHITKARA, J.

 Case no.           Dated          Sections Court
 Complaint          09.08.2008     499, 500, Judicial Magistrate Ist Class, Gurgaon
 No.556 of 2008                    501 IPC   (now Gurugram)

 Criminal Revision No.             Date of Decision    Court
 09 of 2016                        04-06-2018          Additional   Sessions     Judge,
 CIS No. CRR/351/2016                                  Gurugram.
 CNR No.HRGR01-008822-2016

1. The petitioner, an Ex Deputy Resident Editor, (Chandigarh), of the "Indian Express", Chandigarh, aggrieved by the dismissal of the criminal revision petition by the Sessions Court refusing to quash the summons issued in the above-captioned complaint filed for criminal defamation, had come up before this Court by filing the present petition under Section 482 CrPC.

2. As per the pleadings, at the time of publication of the news, the petitioner was working as Deputy News Editor (Chandigarh) in the Indian Express, Chandigarh Edition printed and published by the Indian Express Pvt. Ltd. and the petitioner claims that Indian Express Pvt. Ltd. is the company incorporated under Companies Act, 1956 and is engaged in the publication of newspapers and periodicals across the country. One such 1 1 of 25 ::: Downloaded on - 04-01-2024 23:18:38 ::: Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:000277 CRM-M No. 39409 of 2018 (O&M) publication is the Indian Express newspaper, which prints multi-city/multi-editions. Each publication edition of the newspaper has a designated area where it is printed, published, and circulated. For this reason, each edition is given its address. In para no. 5 of the petition, it has been explicitly claimed that the Chandigarh edition of the newspaper is meant for Chandigarh and adjoining areas of Chandigarh and carries, in addition to National news, news of local interest to Chandigarh and adjoining areas. Petitioner further claims that it is the Delhi edition of The Indian Express, which is circulated in the National Capital Region, viz the metropolitan area encompassing the NCT of Delhi and adjoining urban areas, including Gurgaon. In para no.6, it is further clarified that the local edition, which covers news of local importance, relates to a specific city. The city editions are like pullout supplements with the leading Indian Express newspaper and carry the nomenclature of Newsline preceded by the name of the city, for example, Chandigarh Newsline. In para no.7, the petitioner states that Chandigarh Newsline has a separate registration under the Press and Registration of Books Act, 1857, and in compliance with the said Act, it prints the imprint line of its Editor, Printer, and Publisher. The Chandigarh Newsline dated 17.06.2008, in which the news was published, has a statutory imprint line disclosing the mandatory information, and the petitioner annexed the news item dated 16.06.2008 (Annexure P-1). Varun Chadha published the news item published by Chandigarh Newsline on 17.06.2008.

3. The petitioner is aggrieved by the issuance of summons and the upholding of the said order by the Sessions Court in the above-captioned complaint filed by the respondent, Mr. Param Vir Rathee, IPS, against many journalists and political leaders, in all thirty-four people. The petitioner relies on many grounds, including the issue of cause and jurisdiction, and that even if the complaint is accepted as true, there is still no violation of section 499 IPC, nor did the petitioner act with any malice or intention to defame the complainant. The petitioner's counsel submits that during the interregnum of pendency of this petition, the complainant has settled the matter with some of the respondents; however, no such settlement took place with the petitioner.

4. The respondent-complainant has filed a reply and opposed the present petition because it was the duty of the petitioner to verify the correctness of the news, and without doing so, he let the news printed and published in Indian Express, which caused irreparable loss/damage to the complainant's reputation and petitioner is liable to be prosecuted and punished under Sections 499 and 500 IPC.

5. In the complaint, Annexure P-2, the complainant alleged that he is an IPS Officer 2 2 of 25 ::: Downloaded on - 04-01-2024 23:18:38 ::: Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:000277 CRM-M No. 39409 of 2018 (O&M) of the 1997 batch and belongs to the Haryana cadre. He has been an honest officer, performing his duties with exemplary devotion and sincerity. His Annual Confidential Reports have rated him as an officer of integrity and honesty. At the time of the alleged defamation and the filing of the complaint, he claimed to be posted as Additional Director General of Police (CID), Haryana and asserted that a person of the highest integrity is posted on such a sensitive post as CID Chief of the State. The complainant further stated that he held a good reputation for honesty and integrity; for these reasons, he has earned respect in society, among his colleagues, and the State.

6. As per paragraph no.5 of the complaint, it has been alleged that on June 17, 2008, the complainant noticed a news item in Indian Express with topic: "Accused says he bribed ADGP, sought police protection." The complainant further stated that in the news item, it was reported that Dr. Sandeep Sharma, an accused in the criminal case, had confessed before the Central Bureau of Investigation [CBI] that Param Vir Rathee had recommended Sandeep Sharma's police protection after taking a bribe. In the complaint, the copy of Indian Express dated June 17, 2008, was annexed [Annexure C- 1]. In paragraph seven of the complaint, the complainant further declares that on verification, he came to know that said CBI had not arrested Sandeep Sharma, and as such, his confessing before CBI was out of the question, and consequently, there was no occasion to the complainant recommending his police protection. The next day, the CBI gave a statement, published in the Times of India on June 18, 2008, [C-2]/P-2], in which the CBI clarified this part. In paragraph no. 8, the petitioner mentioned a list of newspapers that had published such news and gave names of eighteen newspapers. In paragraph no. 9 of the complaint, the complainant stated that the imputations contained in the newspapers Annexure P-1, P-3 to P-19 therein showed that the contents were defamatory, which in turn lowered his reputation in the estimation of his friends, colleagues, and public at large, at his place of residence and wherever he served as a police officer. All such reports were factually incorrect because Sandeep Sharma had been provided security keeping in view the threat perception assessed by the District Police, Panchkula, based on the criminal complaint given by Sandeep Sharma wherein he had claimed threats to his life, based on which police registered an FIR. Later, the said FIR was canceled, and his security was withdrawn. Paragraph no. 9 of the complaint explicitly mentioned that the complainant had neither any role in granting such police protection nor Sandeep Sharma had confessed before the CBI because he was never arrested. Those allegations and imputations published against the complainant were factually incorrect and were intentionally made to lower the 3 3 of 25 ::: Downloaded on - 04-01-2024 23:18:38 ::: Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:000277 CRM-M No. 39409 of 2018 (O&M) complainant's credit as a police officer in the estimation of colleagues, friends, and the public.

7. After filing the complaint, the complainant appeared as CW-1 before the concerned Court and reiterated the allegations made in the complaint. It would be appropriate to extract the relevant portion of the said statement, which reads as follows: -

"On 17.06.08, I got mental shock and deep grief after reading an article alongwith my photo, published in an English Daily National Newspaper namely Indian Express. The heading of that news was Accused Says He bribed, ADGP, sought Police Problem. It was published in this article that Accused Dr.Sandeep Sharma has admitted the statement of accused C.B.I. that I (Complainant) have taken bribe from him to provide him police protection. The copy of the newspaper is Ex. C-1 and related newspaper is exhibited at Page-1 of Chandigarh News Line as Ex.C-1/A. This news was clearly the news to cause defamation. This was published with the intent to spoil my self-respect and image. On the next day i.e.on 18.06.08, C.B.I. Has clearly stated through an English National Newspaper Times of India that they have not arrested the accused Dr.Sandeep Sharma."

8. The complainant also examined CW4 Sandeep Khirwal, S.P. Panchkula who testified that Sandeep Sharma had moved an application for threat perception (Ex.24). Based on the threat perception, the Panchkula police appointed one gun man for the personal security of Sandeep Sharma on 14.04.2006 and requisite entries were made in the record. Subsequently, the investigation did not find any substance in the allegation of threat perception and closure report was filed in the said application and consequently, the personal security was withdrawn on 20.09.2007 (i.e. after 01 year 03 months). Referring to the record, CW4 further testified that Sandeep Sharma was given personal security because of the threat perception but later on it was withdrawn because the threat perception was not proved. He explicitly stated that no order was given to him to provide personal security from higher authorities. Thus, through CW4 the complainant tried to prove that the allegations that he had taken bribe from Sandeep Sharma were dis-proved by an IPS rank officer. Panchkula Police had deputed personal security w.e.f. 14-04-2006 to 20-09-2007, thus, CW-4 established that Panchkula police provided security during this period based on threat perception and not because of the complainant's intervention. However, the witness did not prove whether, after 20-09-2007, the Haryana Police had provided any personal security to Sandeep Sharma or not. CW5 testified that 10 cases of fraud committed with bank were registered against Sandeep Sharma. The complainant also examined the Inspector of 4 4 of 25 ::: Downloaded on - 04-01-2024 23:18:38 ::: Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:000277 CRM-M No. 39409 of 2018 (O&M) CBI as CW-3, who testified that Sandeep Sharma was under arrest in another FIR and was lodged in Ambala Jail. He had applied for Sandeep's production warrants on Aug 20, 2008, and interrogated him on Aug 21, 2008; before that, he had not arrested him. Thus, the complainant established by leading evidence that on June 17, 2008, when the news items were published, Sandeep Sharma had not been interrogated or arrested by CBI, and thus, the basis for the news items was false and incorrect. The complainant examined CW-2 & CW-6 to prove that after reading the news in question, the complainant's image and reputation were lowered in their opinion

9. Vide a detailed order dated 17.04.2010, learned Judicial Magistrate Ist Class found prima facie evidence for commission of offence punishable under Section 500 and 501 IPC and accordingly summoned accused no.1 to 34. In the complaint, the petitioner has been arraigned as Accused No.1.

10. The petitioner challenged the summoning order by filing a petition under section 482 CrPC before this court. However, vide order dated 11-05-2016, a co-ordinate bench of this Court relegated the petitioner to the Court of first revision by observing that they should have availed the remedy of criminal revision before the Sessions Court and extended the limitation provided the revision is filed within 30 days. After that, the petitioner challenged the summoning order by filing a criminal revision under section 397 CrPC before the Gurgaon Sessions Court. Vide the impugned judgment dated 04- 06-2018, the Additional Sessions Judge, Gurugram, dismissed the revision petition. It would be appropriate to refer the reasoning given by Additional Sessions Judge which reads as follows: -

"[9]. More so, when any news regarding any person in the authority has been published in public domain without verification of facts and it has been found to be false, it cannot be said that the same has been published in good faith. When the clarification has been given by the CBI in news paper Ex.C2, published on 18.6.2008, it cannot be said on the face of it that the revisionist- accused on earlier occasion had acted without malafide intention. When said accused Sandeep Sharma has not made any statement before CBI and he was not ever been taken in custody by CBI in corruption related matter, the question of suffering of his statement before CBI does not arise at all. At least reasonable enquiry from all the concerned persons should have been made by the revisionist- accused before giving statement and publishing in news paper. Therefore, the learned trial court has rightly appreciated the evidence before summoning the accused. [10]. More so, it is settled law that at the stage of summoning, the Magistrate has to evaluate the material placed before him from the prima- facie view and not from the point of view for 5 5 of 25 ::: Downloaded on - 04-01-2024 23:18:38 ::: Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:000277 CRM-M No. 39409 of 2018 (O&M) conviction or acquittal of the accused. Even otherwise, it has been observed in U.P. Pollution Control Board Vs. M/s. Mohan Meakins Ltd. & ors.,2002(2) RCB. Criminal (421) that;
"In a summoning order, a Magistrate is not required to pass a speaking order but if complaint is dismissed, the Magistrate is to record reasons for dismissal and issuing process."

Similar view has been observed in S.W.P. Palantikar Vs. State of Bihar 2001(4) RCC 437 (SC) and in M/s Pepsi Foods Ltd. & anr. Vs. Special Judicial Magistrate & ors and in Shivjee Singh Versus Nagendra Tiwary and others 2010(2) CCJ 93.

In Bhushan Kumar and another Vs. State (NCT of Delhi) and another 2012(2) RCR (Criminal) 794, Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that:

"Once the Magistrate has exercised his discretion, it is not for the High Court or even Supreme Court to substitute its own discretion for that of the Magistrate or to examine the case on merits".

11. Feeling aggrieved, the petitioner came up before this court by filing this petition under section 482 CrPC, seeking to quash the summoning order and to set aside the dismissal of criminal revision.

12. The petitioner's counsel (without admitting any liability or conceding anything) states that the news report was carried out by Indian Express in good faith in the public interest and based on information provided by CBI officials and their report. Their journalist had not only interacted with the complainant but also mentioned his viewpoint. Neither the newspaper, its reporter, nor the petitioner had made any personal or biased comments.

13. Petitioner's counsel submitted that it is Delhi edition of The Indian Express which is circulated in National Capital Region, viz the metropolitan area encompassing the NCT of Delhi and adjoining urban areas including Gurgaon and the complainant did not lead any evidence to primafacie establish that the newspaper which is published in Gurgaon also carried the same news item because it was Chandigarh Edition, where it was published, which had no circulation in Gurgaon. The Chandigarh edition of the newspaper is meant for Chandigarh and adjoining areas of Chandigarh and carries, in addition to National news, news of local interest to Chandigarh and adjoining areas. The local edition covers news of local importance and relates to a specific city. The city editions are like pullout supplements with the leading Indian Express newspaper and carry the nomenclature of Newsline preceded by the name of the city, for example, Chandigarh Newsline. There is no averment that the complainant and the witnesses had 6 6 of 25 ::: Downloaded on - 04-01-2024 23:18:38 ::: Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:000277 CRM-M No. 39409 of 2018 (O&M) read Chandigarh Newsline. Because the petitioner resided at a place that was beyond the territorial jurisdiction of the Magistrate before whom the complaint was filed, as the mandatory procedure prescribed under Section 202, CrPC was not complied with, and on this ground alone, the summoning order and dismissal of revision deserve to be set aside.

14. The complainant-respondent opposed the present petition and filed his detailed reply. Referring to the reply, the complainant's counsel contended that the newspaper had published a false and defamatory statement. Counsel for the complainant submits that the media must publish reports after verifying their correctness, as any false publication may affect the character and credibility of any respectable person in society. In the present news report, the petitioner did not take any corrective measures despite a clarification issued by the CBI, which was published in Times of India on 18.6.2008, denying the fact of Sandeep Sharma being taken into custody. Despite the clarificatory news published in the Times of India, the petitioner took no corrective measures. The complainant's counsel further submitted that the Magistrate had issued a summon after being fully satisfied and following the procedure under Section 202 CrPC. As such, there is no violation of Section 202 CrPC, and the Magistrate had examined six witnesses, gone through all the evidence, and, on finding sufficient prima facie material and applied his mind.

15. An analysis of the pleadings, the submissions, and the applicability of judicial precedents will lead to the following outcome.

16. On June 17, 2008, the Indian Express, Chandigarh, published the following news report:

Shubham Hospital Case 'Sharma tried to influence officials' Accused says he bribed ADGP, sought police protection Varun Chadha Chandigarh June 16, Additional Director General of Police (Intelligence), Haryana, P. V Rathee, has come under the Central Bureau of Investigation's (CBI) scanner in the Shubham Hospital case after accused Sandeep Sharma confessed on Monday that he had bribed the officer. In return, Rathee had recommended police protection for the accused and provided him with two gunmen of the Haryana Police.
The Shubham Hospital and Diagnostic Centre in Sector 20 Panchkula, was sealed by the police after Sharma's certificates and documents turned out to be 'fake'. Sharma had claimed to possess an MBBS degree as well as an MS in Ophthalmology. He had also availed loans worth crores from different banks with the forged 7 7 of 25 ::: Downloaded on - 04-01-2024 23:18:38 ::: Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:000277 CRM-M No. 39409 of 2018 (O&M) documents.

The gunmen came in handy when Sharma went to the bank or district administration offices to avail loans or get things done. He tried to exert influence on the officials by the these tactics,"

said a CBI Officer.
But Rathee claims he provided the security on the recommendations of district police officials who said Sharma faced "a threat to his life". Sharma confessed to the CBI that his life was not under threat.
Rathee refuted all allegations of receiving money from the accused. "I have never met the person. I don't know why he is leveling such allegations against me," said the ADGP.
On the other hand, SSP Sandeep Khirwar said the police cover was recommended only after Sharma lodged a police complaint against unknown persons threatening him over phone.
Sources claimed no police verification was conducted in the case as a senior police officer had made the recommendations. The accused has named many senior politicians and bureaucrats who used to loan him their official cars when Sharma had to visit the bank. Bank officials also disclosed the names of many senior bureaucrats and politician, who recommended Sharma's name for the loans, to the CBI. In March 2007, Punjab and Sind Bank officials reportedly went to him when they fell short of their annual investment target by Rs.5 Crore. "He called up an IAS officer of Haryana Dairy Development Federation Corporation and ordered him to deposit the money with the bank to oblige the bank officials. The very next day the money was deposited in the bank. Later, the IAS Officer forced the bank officials to pass a loan of the accused," bank officials told the CBI.
CBI officials said they will ask the bureaucrats and politicians named by the accused to join investigations after verifying the facts. "But one thing is certain many politicians and bureaucrats will find themselves in trouble soon." said a senior CBI Officer.

17. On June 18, 2008, the Times of India published a news report containing the following clarification from CBI:

No record of accused bribing ADGP, says CBI TIMES NEWS NETWORK Chandigarh: The central bureau of investigation (CBI), on Tuesday, said Dr Sandeep Sharma, accused in the Shubham Hospital case, hadn't given any statement to the investigation agency claiming that he had bribed an additional director general of police (ADGP) for getting security. "There is nothing on record about the accused bribing any Haryana police official. The accused, Dr. Sandeep Sharma is in Ambala Central Jail and yet to be taken into CBI custody" said a DIG rank official of CBI.
However, sources in the crime branch of Haryana police maintained that the accused had been provided security in 2006 after he lodged an FIR in Sector 20 police station, alleging threat to his life.
According to the FIR, which was registered on the 8 8 of 25 ::: Downloaded on - 04-01-2024 23:18:38 ::: Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:000277 CRM-M No. 39409 of 2018 (O&M) complaint of accused doctor, he had received threat calls from a Shimla based STD. However, the first information report was later cancelled.

The crime branch official maintained that a report -

mentioning how Sharma obtained security - was sent to senior police officials in Haryana police headquarter, sector 6, two months back. Apart from this, Sharma had also filed an application regarding police security in the office of Haryana chief minister.

A senior Haryana police official claimed that during the interrogation Sharma had made several claims like gifting a Scorpio to a senior politician of Punjab and bribing a number of senior medical officials and politicians but had failed to provide any proof.

18. In Shatrughna Prasad Sinha v. Rajbhau Surajmal Rathi, (1996) 6 SCC 263, Supreme Court holds, [13]. ...It is the settled legal position that a Court has to read the complaint as a whole and find out whether allegations disclosed constitute an offence under Section 499 triable by the Magistrate.

19. The relevant portion of the complaint reads as follows:

... [5]. That on 17.06.2008 the complainant was shocked and deeply hurt to see a news item appearing in the "Indian Express" an English National Daily with a title "Accused says he bribed ADGP, sought police protection" along with a photograph of the complainant. In the said news item it was reported that one Dr. Sandeep Sharma, an accused in a criminal case, has confessed before the Central Bureau of Investigation that the complainant had recommended police protection to the said accused after taking bribe. A copy of the said news item which appeared in the "Indian Express" English National daily newspaper dated 17.06.2008 is being annexed herewith as Annexure P-1.

[6]. That the news item annexure P-1 is per-se defamatory. A bare reading of the news item makes it abundantly clear that the imputations made therein have intended to lower the reputation of the complainant in the estimation of everybody whoever happens to read the same. [7]. It is not that the complainant has to bring only two witnesses to support his allegations in the complaint to have the criminal law set into motion. The order of the Magistrate summoning the accused must reflect that he has applied his mind to the facts of the case and the law applicable thereto. case_summary: In Shobhana Bhartia And Ors. vs The State Of U.P. (2024), the applicants, including Shobhana Bhartia, Chairperson of HT Media Ltd., filed an application under Section 482 of the Criminal Procedure Code (Cr.P.C.) to quash the proceedings initiated under Sections 500, 501, and 502 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) for defamation. The complaint, filed by a former District Judge, alleged that a defamatory news item was published on the Hindustan Times website in June 2017, accusing the judge of being involved in a questionable bail decision. The applicants argued that the news item was published in good faith, based on authentic information from communication between the High Court and the Supreme Court.
case_decision: The Allahabad High Court, after reviewing the case, quashed the defamation proceedings. The court held that the publication of the news item was covered under Exceptions 1 and 3 of Section 499 IPC, which allow the publication of truthful information in the public interest and good faith opinions on matters of public concern. Since the communication between the High Court and the Supreme Court, which formed the basis of the news item, was authentic and undisputed, the court ruled that the applicants had no intention to harm the complainant's reputation. Therefore, the complaint was deemed an abuse of legal provisions, and the proceedings were quashed.

It has been submitted by the learned Senior Counsel that in the present era, media has a very important role to play in the democracy by highlighting the deeds and misdeeds of the Government as well as Public authorities. It has next been submitted that there is no derogatory words in the news item against any person. The said news items were published in the news paper on 19.06.2017 on the basis of the substance of the aforesaid correspondence in between two Constitutional Authorities.

Thereafter, on 26.05.2017, private respondent was transferred to District Chandauli and he took charge as District & Sessions Judge there on 03.06.2017. Respondent no. 2, after his superannuation on 31.08.2017, legal notice was sent alleging publication of alleged defamatory news on 15th September, 2017. It has been submitted that the reply to the said notices was also given. Thereafter, on 16th November, 2017, Complaint No. 2800 of 2017 was filed and statement of the complainant/respondent no. 2 was recorded under Section 200 Cr.P.C. In his statement, respondent no. 2 stated that only with the intention to harm his reputation, the said news item was published, due to which, his image was tarnished. In the aforesaid statement, respondent no. 2 also stated that by way of notice, he asked from the applicants about the press note of the High Court as well as the Intelligence Bureau report, being not available with him, but the same was not provided.
8. Thereafter, statements of Mr. Purnendra Kumar Srivastava and Shri V.K. Dubey, Retired H.J.S. Officer were recorded under Section 202 Cr.P.C. It has been submitted by the learned counsel for the applicants that general statement was made under Section 202 Cr.P.C. by the witnesses that the private respondent was honest and reputed Officer of his cadre and belongs to a reputed family background and after publishing the news items, his image was tarnished in their eyes.
9. It has further been submitted by the learned counsel for the applicants that as by way of notice, the correspondence in between the High Court and Hon'ble Supreme Court was asked by the complainant, the copy of the same was already provided to him after passing of the order dated 24th January, 2018 by this Court in Application u/s 482 Cr.P.C. No. 80 of 2018, but no rebuttal about the contents of the letter is made by the private respondent in the counter affidavit filed by him in the said application or in the present case. He also relied on the decision of Queens Bench in the case of Scot Vs. Sampson, 1882 9 QB 491 and submitted that defamation in simplest way is a false statement to a man to his discredit'. This definition is smaller yet it encompasses everything about the concept. It has also been submitted that to constitute 'defamation under Section 499 I.P.C., there must be an imputation and such imputation must have been made with the intention of harming or knowing or having reason to believe that it will harm the reputation of the person about whom it is made. It would be sufficient to show that the accused intended or knew or had reason to believe that the imputation made by him would harm the reputation of complainant, irrespective of whether complainant actually suffered directly or indirectly from the imputation. It has, thus, been submitted that the impugned proceedings are liable to be quashed.
12. It has further been submitted that the respondent no. 2 applied for the alleged privileged communication between this Court and Hon'ble Supreme Court dated 3rd May, 2017 under the provisions of Right to Information Act, but he could not succeed. 13. It has vehemently been submitted that the applicants are also liable to be prosecuted under the provisions of Official Secrets Act. While submitting that all these arguments raised by the learned counsel for the applicants may be ventilated before the court below at appropriate stage, it has been submitted that the present application is liable to be dismissed.

I have considered the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the applicants, learned counsel for the respondent and gone through the contents of the application, counter affidavit, rejoinder affidavit, statements recorded under Section 200 and 202 Cr.P.C. as well as other relevant documents and the office copy of letter dated 03.05.2017 placed by Senior Registrar of this Court.
15. It is evident from the record that the photocopy of the privileged communication placed by the applicants before this Court on 24.01.2018 was provided to the private respondent. It is further evident that the allegations made in the complaint against the applicants and other accused persons is of tacit consent and criminal conspiracy for commission of the offence of defamation.
16. 'Defamation' is defined in Section 499 I.P.C., which clearly provides that whoever, by words either spoken or intended to be read, or by signs or by visible representations, makes or publishes any imputation concerning any person intending to harm, or knowing or having reason to believe that such imputation will harm the reputation of such person, is said, except in the cases mentioned in the Exception clauses.
17. Admittedly, in the present case, the news items were published on 19th June, 2017. Thereafter, notice was given by the private respondent and asked the copy of the privileged communication as well as Intelligence Bureau report. It is evident from the record that the photocopy of the privileged communication was placed by the learned counsel for the applicants before this Court on 24.01.2018 in Application u/s 482 No. 80 of 2018 and under the order of this Court of the date, the copy of the same was provided to the private respondent. The inclination of respondent no. 2 appears to be that for publishing a confidential communication, all the accused persons are liable to be prosecuted under the provisions of Official Secrets Act, 1923.
18. Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Jawaharlal Dadra & Ors. Vs. Manoharrao Ganpatrao Kapsikar & Anr., (1998) 4 SCC 112, held that in the case of accurate and true reporting published in good faith, it cannot be said that the accused intended to harm the reputation of the complainant. Para 5 (relevant) of the said decision is as under :
"It is quite apparent that what the accused had published in its newspaper was an accurate and true report of the proceedings of the Assembly. Involvement of the respondent was disclosed by the preliminary enquiry made by the Government. If the accused bona fide believing the version of the Minister to be true published the report in good faith it cannot be said that they intended to harm the reputation of the complainant. It was a report in respect of public conduct of public servants who were entrusted with public funds intended to be used for public good. Thus the facts and circumstances of the case disclose that the news items were published for public good. All these aspects have been overlooked by the High Court."

19. Indisputably, the privileged correspondence between the High Court and Hon'ble Supreme Court is not denied by respondent no. 2.

20. In view of above facts and discussions, this Court is of the view that the action of the applicants is squarely covered in the Exception (1) & (3) of Section 499 I.P.C. Section 499 along with Exception (1) & (3) is reproduced hereunder :

"First Exception:- Imputation of truth which public good requires to be made or published:- It is not defamation to impute anything which is true con-cerning any person, if it be for the public good that the imputation should be made or published. Whether or not it is for the public good is a question of fact.
Third Exception:- Conduct of any person touching any public question:- It is not defamation to express in good faith any opinion whatever respecting the conduct of any person touching any public question, and respecting his character, so far as his character appears in that conduct, and no further."

21. In view of the above facts and discussions, this Court is of the view that the complaint in question is nothing but a sheer abuse of the legal provisions and no offence, as alleged, can be said to be made out.

22. The impugned proceedings are hereby quashed. The application stands allowed.

23. Office is directed to communicate this order to the court below, forthwith.

Order Date :- 22 December, 2023.

V. Sinha"

case_summary: In the case Mihir Diwakar And Another vs Mahendra Singh Dhoni And Others (2024), the plaintiffs, Mihir Diwakar and another, filed a suit seeking an injunction and damages against Mahendra Singh Dhoni (Defendant No. 1) and other media houses (Defendant Nos. 2 to 35) for allegedly publishing false and defamatory content. The plaintiffs argued that the defendants had defamed them through various media reports. The plaintiffs sought to restrain the defendants from further publishing such content. The counsel for Defendant No. 20, ANI Media Pvt. Ltd., argued that the suit was not maintainable and relied on the Delhi High Court judgment in Veer Arjun Newspaper Private Limited v. Bahori Lal & Ors. (2013), which held that reporting factual matters, such as the contents of complaints or legal proceedings, as part of journalistic activity does not amount to defamation. The reporting was covered under the exception to Section 499 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC), which protects truthful reporting of judicial proceedings from defamation claims.
case_decision: The Delhi High Court, presided by Justice Prathiba M. Singh, scheduled the next hearing for January 29, 2024, and directed the Registry to inform Defendant No. 1 (Mahendra Singh Dhoni) about the case. The court acknowledged the argument made by Defendant No. 20, stating that the report merely covered the proceedings of a criminal case filed by Dhoni against the plaintiffs in Ranchi, and thus might be protected under the exception to defamation in the IPC. The court will further examine the maintainability of the suit and whether any injunction should be granted in the subsequent hearings.

If it were to be held otherwise, it would result in nothing but the final result of all enquiries/disputes/judgments being published in the newspapers and the patrons of said newspapers being denied the knowledge of the complaints/disputes pending for enquiry/adjudication. 9. He further submits that his client is fully protected under the exception to Section 499 of Indian Penal Code as the reporting merely covers the proceeding pending in the criminal case filed by Defendant No.1 against the Plaintiffs which is pending in Ranchi.

10. List on 29th January, 2024 in the supplementary list.

PRATHIBA M. SINGH, J.

case_summary: In Vijaya Babu S vs Divya (O.S.No.6869/2016), the plaintiff, Vijaya Babu, sought Rs. 25 lakhs in compensation, alleging defamation and mental agony caused by false molestation accusations made by the defendant, Divya. The plaintiff claimed that the defendant lodged a frivolous complaint with both the Brigade Gateway Apartment Owners Association and the Subramanyanagar police, accusing him of molesting her in the apartment parking lot. The plaintiff maintained that the allegations were fabricated, as verified by CCTV footage, and had tarnished his reputation, both personally and professionally, causing severe social and mental distress.
case_decision: The court ruled in favor of the plaintiff, finding that the defendant's complaint was false and defamatory, with intent to harm the plaintiff's reputation. The court awarded Rs. 25 lakhs as compensation for the damage caused to the plaintiff's reputation and the mental agony suffered. The defendant was ordered to pay this amount within 60 days, with an additional 12% interest accruing if the payment was delayed beyond the specified time.

                       JUDGMENT

The plaintiff's suit for compensation for an amount of Rs.25 lakhs for causing damages and loss to his reputation, also causing mental agony by the defendants 3 O.S.No.6869/2016 by lodging false, frivolous complaint before the Subramanyanagar police station and in the Management Committee of Brigade Gateway Apartment Owners Association alleging that, he has committed the offence of molestation on the defendant No.1, by tearing her cloth and even assaulted on her.

2. The brief facts of the plaintiff's case is as follows :-

i) The plaintiff is a resident of Bengalurian, he is working as a Director of Sap Labs India Private Ltd., since 9 years.
ii) The plaintiff and defendants were neighbours in Brigade Gateway Apartment. The children of both the plaintiff and defendants were attending the same school and common study circle fir their academic. It is both the plaintiff and defendants were sharing the responsibility of pick up and drop the both the children alternatively. The plaintiff alleged that, the defendants 4 O.S.No.6869/2016 have started shirking away from their responsibility Temporary Injunction pick up and drop their children, when their turn comes, for which the plaintiff and his wife have informed the defendants to drop and pick up their children on their own both from school and study circle, which had triggered to strain their relationship very badly, for which the defendants have started abuse the plaintiff and his wife in the presence of their children, stating that the plaintiff is not belongs to civilized community. Prior to that children both the side used to mingle freely, used play together and used to stay in ones house very often.
iii). The plaintiff used leave home regularly at 6.30 a.m. On 25/9/2015 as usual, he left his home, he went to the parking lot bearing No.G-622, with his car when he started to move on the ramp to take an exit, by that time the 1st defendant deliberately came in front of the vehicle, stood on the middle of the ramp, stopped the 5 O.S.No.6869/2016 plaintiff's car, she started to do jumping, screaming and abusing the plaintiff in filthily. Further, she tore the back of her cloth. Despite all these, the plaintiff did not get down from the car, some how he move away,when he reached to the Boom barrier on the milk colony gate of the apartment, there the security stopped him and told that somebody is calling him. Accordingly plaintiff came back, by that time the 1st defendant deliberately by showing her torn clothes, shouting on the plaintiff and alleging that its the plaintiff molested her by tearing her cloth and assaulted on her, by doing so outraged her modesty. Thereafter, the defendant No.1 lodged a complaint before the Management Committee and also before the Subramanyanagar police station.
iv) He alleged that, the police have called him regularly regularly from 26th to 29th September 2015 on the guise of inquiry. Despite pleading innocence, they started to see him in a suspicious manner by alleging 6 O.S.No.6869/2016 without an no woman will lodge false complaint that too allegation of molestation. An atmosphere being created that he has committed a serious offence, news was spread in the community that due to commission of serious offence, case got registered and police will take him to custody. Despite the plaintiff requested the police to verify the CCTV footage to know the true fact they neglected his requests. By that time, he sensed that on a false case, he will be put into trouble by arrest, he contacted the counsel to file a petition to seek an anticipatory bail and with kept the surety ready, in the event the bail granted on condition.
v). Based on the complaint of the defendant no.1, the Brigade Gateway Residents Welfare Association, which is a registered body of owners and residents of said apartment consisting of 1255 flats and 13 blocks, the Management Committee consisting 13 elected members from various block have called the plaintiff, read out the 7 O.S.No.6869/2016 charges made against him. But the plaintiff refuted all the charges as false and created. But nobody were ready to listen to his case, started to look him in a suspicious manner, as the allegations are serious nature, which is allegedly committed on an woman in a cellar are of the parking slot, which has hurted his sentiments. The people in the community started to murmuring on an incident, he overheard the allegation that how a man in a decent look and so much reputation can involve in such offence, that too in a protected environment. On the false complaint, the Committee called the plaintiff to face an enquiry, which has caused serious embarrassment on him and on his family.
vi). After receiving the complaint, the Managing Committee has verified the CCTV footage fixed in the parking slot of L-Block right side. Upon watching the CCTV footage, they found that on 25/9/2015 the 1 st defendant on first time entered the parking slot at 6.22 8 O.S.No.6869/2016 a.m. Again at 6.43.03 a.m. by watching that the plaintiff in his car is reaching towards towards the ramp, she went in hide behind the pillar at L-Block, when the plaintiff started to move his car, the defendant came on the center of the ramp, by that time the plaintiff honked by requesting the defendant to leave the way to move out, but the 1st defendant no.1 turning back, run down towards his car started to tear her cloths and abused the plaintiff in filthy language. Despite the provocation made by the defendant No.1, he did not get down from the vehicle at all. Thereafter she rushed towards the Reception, through the security called her husband the defendant No.2 and their maid Jayalakshmi, before whom the defendant No.1 briefed facts which are laced with the false facts, stating that its the plaintiff molested her in the parking slot, teared clothe, by doing so caused outrage to her modesty. By considering the condition of the defendant No.1, where her clothes teared thus her 9 O.S.No.6869/2016 maid offered her duppata. Thereafter they proceed to their home. In the CCTV footage of the Lift, the defendant No.1 was crying, where the defendant No.2 wiped her tears. For which the plaintiff contended that, the defendants have made all these with intent to fix the plaintiff in a false case of molestation, made serious serious allegation to put the plaintiff in a state of guilt, to face the mental trauma, societal outrage on him, to made belittle in the eye of the public. By doing so, the defendants have deliberately imputed the reputation, moral and intellectual character of the plaintiff in the eyes of the public.
vii). The plaintiff contended that the defendants are well educated, living in a civilized society were aware about the consequences of lodging of false complaint such as allegation of causing molestation to an woman, as in view of amendment to the criminal law of this country, in particularly for the Section 354 of IPC, for the 10 O.S.No.6869/2016 act of molestation on a woman is a serious offence.
viii). Due to the act of the defendants which has caused severe loss and injury to the status of the plaintiff, his reputation got severely lowered in front of the society, particularly in the community of the Brigade Gateway apartment made him to live under a nightmare until knowing the truth by watching the CCTV footage.

Due to the act of the defendants the perception of the people on the plaintiff got changed. They started to look him in a suspicious manner.

ix). The President of the Brigade Gateway Owners Association after watching the CCTV footage directed the defendant No.1 to withdraw her complaint both from the Association as well as police station. In this regard he gave a letter addressing both the parties holding that the case of the defendant No.1 is false and the plaintiff is an innocent of the accused. The defendant No.1 by noticing the fact that nobody is buying her false story, went to the 11 O.S.No.6869/2016 police station and withdrawn her complaint, based on which the police called the plaintiff, took his statement and informed him that the case is closed as the defendant No.1 withdrawn her complaint as not pressed. As the act of the defendant No.1 was so serious, caused lot of imputation to his character and reputation, thus he issued the notice by seeking the defendant No.1 to seek an unconditional apology. But wherein the defendant No.1 issued reply arrogantly contending that the plaintiff should have shown an appreciation on the defendant No.1 for withdrawing her complaint by showing sympathy on him rather condemning her issuing the reply and alleging that he is making the mountain out of mole hill. For which the plaintiff alleged that the defendant No.1 shown no remorse to her act, she went on instigating and provoking the plaintiff. However the defendant No.1 in her reply had categorically admitted lodging of complaint before both the Police and Managing Committee of 12 O.S.No.6869/2016 Brigade Gateway Apartment Owners Association and withdrawal of the same. The plaintiff contended that he is a Director working for Multinational Company in a reputed post for whom the defendants managed to circulate the false information, where the management of his Employer company had sought the clarification on the issue. On the allegation, even his employer were looking very suspiciously, until clearing of the cloud of doubt created on his character. Based on the complaint of defendant, the police have harassed the plaintiff by calling him to the police station repeatedly, have created the shadow of arrest, making his life very bleak. By lodging the complaint before the Managing Committee, where the plaintiff and his family members were subjected for inquiry. The defendants have circulated false facts among the community. The plaintiff was an honest, and he is an intellectual among the community in the Brigade Gateway apartment owners association, 13 O.S.No.6869/2016 consisting of many CEOs of Software companies, senior bureaucrats like IAS, IPS and IFS. Infact the plaintiff had an idea to contest for the managing committee of the apartment owners association. The complaint of the defendant, has ruined his opportunity. Thus he could not contest the election by participating in the AGM.

x). The plaintiff contended that, his wife is also a reputed personality in the community. The members used to invite her for weekend get together and used to call her for discussion. Immediately after this incident, they stopped to invite her and she has faced serious embarrassment. Even his children have faced such situation, for no mistake of them. As the community have started to isolate them, by restricting their children not to mingle with the children of the plaintiff for play and other activities. They underwent serious trauma.

xi). The plaintiff contended that for taking the criminal action against the defendant he has aready 14 O.S.No.6869/2016 lodged a complaint in PCR No.15167/2015 under Section 200 of Cr.P.C for committing the offences under Section 211, 499 and 500 r/w. 34 of IPC. The jurisdictional Magistrate after taking cognizance forwarded the complaint to the jurisdictional Subramanyanagar police station to investigate the case. Accordingly the police have received the complaint registered the case in their Crime No.159/2016. Thus the plaintiff contended that in the present case, he has restricted his case only for causing the damages to his character and reputation.

3. After service of summons, the defendants have appeared through their counsel and filed their written statement by denying the entire averment of the plaint as false. But they admitted that initially they were sharing the cordial relationship. They used to pick up and drop their children alternatively both from the school and study circle, but that cannot be termed as responsibility, dereliction of duty and shirking away from the 15 O.S.No.6869/2016 responsibility. They contended that, the plaintiff and defendants are neigbhours in Brigade Gateway apartment, on account of trivial and in-consequential incidents, their relationship got strained. Misunderstanding have been crept, have lost the mutual trust, as mistrust took the dominance. Each one have started to look other exaggeratedly in a suspicion manner, started entertaining the ideas which are trying to destroy other, which is nothing but a physiological fact that, culminated in things which are unpleasant thereby the defendants vacated the flat situated at Brigade Gateway and moved away.

4. On the incident dated 25/9/2015 is concerned, the defendants have contended that as on that day, the defendant No.1 after her morning walk while returning, it was severely felt by her that the plaintiff attacked her, which resulted in tearing of her clothes and further when he refused to stop his car, 16 O.S.No.6869/2016 despite of her request fortified the feeling that plaintiff must be the reason for the incident, immediately she brought the same into the notice of the managing committee and on the very next day she lodged a formal complaint with the jurisdictional police with a request to police to advice the plaintiff to mend his ways. She further contended that, on the advise of the Managing Committee and the jurisdictional police, the 1 st defendant wanted to bury the same, she immediately withdrew the complaint, with a fond hopes that the strained relationship between the plaintiff and defendants may patch up. The withdrawal of the complaint was unconditional, the plaintiff should have taken the same in right spirit. He should have taken out all the ill feelings by giving a decent burial. But the plaintiff distorted the facts, filed this false suit. She denied that based on her complaint the Managing Committee did not conduct an enquiry and no such embarrassment being 17 O.S.No.6869/2016 caused to the family of the plaintiff. As she withdrew the complaint immediately on the next day after the incident, thus the police did not call the plaintiff for interrogation and at no point of time they made him to sit in the police station and no shadow of registration of case and arrest being created. No damage being caused to his family within the community of Brigade Gateway Apartment. The plaintiff is an introvert, less familiar, not even known by the occupants of L-Block Apartment in the Brigade Gateway Apartment. The defendants have not spread any thing on this incident with in the community. They contended that, the Brigade Gateway Apartment is consisting of 1255 flats, multi level parking area and it has been closely observing through the circulated CCTV. Further she denied that as on the incident she had knowledge on existence of Section 354 of IPC, thus she had no intention to take any of its advantage. She denied doing any problem pursuant to the incident as the same 18 O.S.No.6869/2016 was not warranted to her and she was not in need of any sympathy. The defendants contended that the plaintiff has filed the false suit, which deserves to be dismissed with cost.

5. By considering the pleadings of the parties, this court was pleased to frame following issues.

1. Whether the defendant has caused defamation to the name and image of the plaintiff by falsely implicating him in a Criminal complaint and deliberately causing defamation by filing complaint before the Brigade Gateway Residents Welfare Association?

2. Whether there was loss of reputation of the plaintiff?

3. What amount of compensation, the plaintiff is entitled to?

Note: Issue no. 3 is stricken out, and to recasted the same as herein below:

Issue No. 3: Does the plaintiff proves that the defendant no.1's complaint damages his reputation both in personal and public life, thus compensation of 25,00,000/- is requires to be 19 O.S.No.6869/2016 awarded?

4. What rate of interest the plaintiff is entitled to?

5. What order?

6. The plaintiff in order to prove his case, examined himself as PW.1 and produced in all 13 documents which are marked as Ex.P1 to P13 and examined Ex-President of Brigade Gateway Apartment Owners Association as P.W.2 and the Assistant Manager of Brigade Gateway Apartment as P.W.3.

7. The defendant No.1 was examined as DW.1 and Ex.D1 got marked. As she failed to appear before the Court for facing the cross examination, thus her evidence has been discarded.

8. Heard the arguments of both the learned counsel for the plaintiff and defendants.

9. The plaintiff has filed written arguments and in support of his arguments placed reliance on the decision. The defendants have also placed their reliance on the 20 O.S.No.6869/2016 decisions sited in the list.

10. My finding on the above issues are :-

Issue No.1: In the affirmative Issue No.2: In the affirmative Issue No.3: In the affirmative Issue No.4: As per the discussion and final order Issue No.5: As per final order, for the following:-
REASONS

11. Issue No.1 & 2 : Plaintiff filed the present suit for damages on the ground that the defendant No.1 with intend to damage his reputation in the eye of public, within in the vicinity of Brigade apartment community consisting of more than 1300 fltas and also with in the professional circle. Created the sequence, as if the plaintiff molested her in a parking slot by tearing her clothes attempted to commit serious offence on an woman. Orchestrated the incident, spread the false 21 O.S.No.6869/2016 propaganda, took the incident to the next level by lodging complaint before the Executive committee of the Brigade apartment owners association and even lodged a complaint before the the Subramanyanagar police station.

12. Its the plaintiff's case is that, On 25/9/2015 as usual, he left his home, he went to the parking lot bearing No.G-622, with his car when he started to move on the ramp to take an exit, by that time the 1 st defendant deliberately came in front of the vehicle, stood on the middle of the ramp, stopped the plaintiff's car, she started to do jumping, screaming and abusing the plaintiff in filthily. Further, she tore the back of her cloth. Despite all these, the plaintiff did not get down from the car, some how he move away,when he reached to the Boom barrier on the milk colony gate of the apartment, there the security stopped him and told that somebody is calling him. Accordingly plaintiff came back, by that 22 O.S.No.6869/2016 time the 1st defendant deliberately by showing her tored clothes, shouting on the plaintiff and alleging that its the plaintiff molested her by tearing her cloth and assaulted on her, by doing so outraged her modesty. Thereafter, the defendant No.1 lodged a complaint before the Management Committee and also before the Subramanyanagar police station.

13. It is not in dispute that the Brigade Gateway Apartment complex consisting of 1255 flats and the plaintiff and defendants are residents of L-Block in the same floor, they were neighboured and they were maintaining a cordial relationship as their children were studying and attending the same school and they were playing together, sharing food, used to sleep together sometime. But due to some misunderstanding crept in them, with regard to drop and pick up their children from the school and study circle. Its the plaintiff contention that differences due to the conduct of the 23 O.S.No.6869/2016 defendants, as they shifted their responsibility to pick up and dropping their children to the plaintiff, to shirk away from sharing their responsibility to do the same in alternatively. When the plaintiffs reminded the defendants to let us drop up and pick up their children, for which the defendant no.1 condemned on the mindset of the plaintiff's wife, which triggered to hate to each other. Infact the defendants in their written statements have explained what ruined their relationship, and where that led and what happened in the end. Its relevant to refer evidence of the P.W.No.1 deposed in the cross examination;

"Around 2014 I might have told to the defendants that they are not doing their duty in picking and dropping of defendant's children. For the said defendants have reacted in a rude manner. After that I stopped to pick up and drop the defendant's chidlren. Its is true to suggest that it is the breaking point of our family myself and defendant family in continuing the the cordiality. It is true to 24 O.S.No.6869/2016 suggest the at earlier to this incident, children of both the family were used to play together, study together and eat together. It is true to suggest that there after both of us advised our respective children to maintain the distance.

14. Further, If the circumstances explained by the plaintiff and defendants are read, defendants have started to taunting on him making sarcastic incidents the moment the plaintiff stepped out to go to his employment in the early morning, the defendant used to bang their door by making some unhealthy conduct. In this regard, its relevant to extract the same to under that the gravity of the circumstances existed between these two family:

Its it true to suggest that while I passing infront of defendant's apartment, they used to bang their door. It is true to suggest that I never bothered why the defendants were banging on their doors. And, this was happening for period of more than 5-6 months. It is false suggest that without ascertaining the reason for 25 O.S.No.6869/2016 banging the door by defendants I came to the conclusion that it was against me"

15. If the above suggestions are read, no one will bang their door. Whatever may be the reasons. That too, whenever the plaintiff is moving right infront of it. Which is nothing but the sadist mentality. Which shows the the level of mindset displayed by the defendants. How low in their contentment.

16. With regard to incident dated. 25.9.2015 concerned, the defendant No.1 on 25/9/2015 lodged a complaint with the Managing Committee of the Brigade Gateway Apartment Association as per Ex.2 alleging that on 25/9/2015 at about 6.40 a.m. in the ground level parking lot, the plaintiff herein attacked on her, teared her clothes and tried to fled away with his car, but she stopped him with the help of the securities. Thus she had requested the Association to take necessary actions, failing which she warned to initiate the legal proceedings. 26 O.S.No.6869/2016

17. It is not in dispute that the defendant No.1 also lodged the complaint with the jurisdictional Subramanyanagar police station as per Ex.P1 dated 26/9/2015, wherein she has alleged that since quite some time it is the plaintiff and his wife causing physical and mental harassment to them and yesterday at 6.45 a.m. after completion of her morning walk when she was going to home, in the parking slot of their apartment, all of a sudden the plaintiff came behind her, attacked on her, teared her cloths and later when she cried, he fled away with his car . She by screaming loudly with the help of the security stopped his car and later there was a discussion in the presence of the management committee to resolve the dispute, thus there is a delay in lodging the complaint. By alleging many things she has lodged the said complaint.

18. It is not in dispute that the Management Committee of Brigade Gateway Apartment Owners 27 O.S.No.6869/2016 Association has sought an explanation from the plaintiff, who gave his explanation as per Ex.P3 by denying all the allegations made by the defendant No.1 herein and he had requested the Management Committee to conduct a thorough investigation to absolve him from the alleged allegation and it is not in dispute that the defendant No.1 had withdrawn her complaint from the Subramanyanagar police station by giving her statement as per Ex.P4 stating that, as the Management Committee of Brigade Gateway Apartment Owners Association has resolved their dispute and made them to live peacefully, thus she sought the permission to withdraw her complaint to close them as not pressed.

19. It is not in dispute that, even the police have took the statement of the plaintiff on 29/9/2015 stating that he has not committed any molestation of the defendant No.1 herein. It is not in dispute that the plaintiff got issued the notice as per Ex.P5 dated 28 O.S.No.6869/2016 3/11/2015, sought an unconditional apology from the defendant No.1 herein and also to make compensation of Rs.10 lakhs within 15 days for causing him to undergo a traumatic condition due to the false allegation of molestation and lodging of complaint before both the Brigade Gateway Apartment Owners Association and also before the jurisdictional police. It is not in dispute that the defendants have issued a reply as per Ex.P6, under which the defendants have tried to make out a case that the lodging of the complaint is only a trivialities, it happened in a normal wear and tear of life and informed him not to blow the same out of proportionate and tried to make out that the case of the plaintiff as distorted and exaggerated. It is the plaintiff's contention is that, as the matter did not settled amicably, thus he also lodged the complaint before the jurisdictional Magistrate for taking criminal action and he has approached this court by filing the present suit by seeking damages and 29 O.S.No.6869/2016 compensation.

20. The case of the plaintiff is an undisputed fact. As the defendant No.1 admitted the fact that she on 25/9/2015 lodged her complaint against the plaintiff alleging that he attacked on her, torn her clothes, caused molestation and in this regard she lodged the complaint before both the management committee of Brigade Gateway Apartment Owners Association and Subramanyanagara police station and she also admitted that she has withdrawn both the complaints. But her case is that, she lodged the complaint purely on the ground that she was under some illusion. Later she realized her mistakes, on the advice of the management committee, she withdrew the same with intent to bridge relationship between the plaintiff and defendants. Even she asked the plaintiff to bury the incident, from complaint as no harm has been caused to the plaintiff personally, professionally, family and in social life. In 30 O.S.No.6869/2016 fact, they have expected the plaintiff to behave maturely, he should have appreciated her for withdrawing the complaint. But the plaintiff without burying the same, making the mole out of mountain. He exaggerated the facts and distorted the facts. Thus the suit of the plaintiff deserves to be dismissed.

21. There is a place to purchase such products, but they do not invest time to find out the true story, as the true facts has carries no curiosity. The sound created from the lodging of the complaint would not have been doused by just withdrawing the same. The impact created from lodging the complaint may not be proportionate while withdrawing the same. As the allegations finds a curiosity but not the innocence. It is necessary to see the case of the plaintiff in an empathetic manner. The reputation is a most valuable asset of any individual, the moment it destroys, it is too difficult to buy back in any manner and means. The reputation is an intangible asset 45 O.S.No.6869/2016 of every individual, he will be in the society until he carries the same reputation, the moment its defaces, would be thrown into the dustbin, irrespective of any amount of good work done in his life time. The allegations made out with an innocence can be ignored. But where the allegations made with intention with a pre-meditated plan, with a clear definition to cause damage to the reputation of innocent man cannot be considered very lightly, who is an evil minded character, who deserves for punishment. Thus this Court is of the considered opinion that the act of the defendant No.1 was an intentional one, preplanned, clearly with intentions to disrepute the character of the plaintiff in the society. Thus answered issue No.1 and 2 in the affirmative.

33. Issue No.3 and 4 : Character is a one's reputation, which is an invaluable one, which cannot be purchased by using the money and material, it is gained 46 O.S.No.6869/2016 by ones own hardship, it is continuous, consistent, which is the most difficult task in the present society. To maintain and to develop such a character, one has to live like sage to reach to that level, one has to cross most difficult sphere of life. Wherein this Court found that the defendant No.1 with an evil mindset had decided to destroy the reputation of the plaintiff, such an act cannot be allowed to be swallowed easily and cannot be considered casually and it cannot be allowed go unnoticeable and it cannot be ignored without punishing the person who plotted it and the guilty should be punished that must be a lesson to think twice before doing all these in their lifetime.

34. Admittedly both the plaintiff and defendants were residing in a sophisticated society consisting of class of people, intellectual, highly notable people where even a small mistake of the person will be put him in isolation from the society. The act of the defendant No.1 47 O.S.No.6869/2016 cannot be considered leniently and lightly. Further, really the plaintiff is not blowing out of proportion. He has not exaggerated facts, he is trying to get a justice to trauma he faced. Thus, this Court is of the opinion that the plaintiff sought Rs.25 lakhs as damages and compensation for causing disreputation, which appears to be very reasonable. Thus plaintiff is entitled for the compensation of Rs.25 Lakhs sought in the suit. This court found no reasons to reduce the same. As the character is invaluable. Once lost, no amount of money will bring back the same. The Character is like a pure white clothes, any amount of stains can be easily noticeable. There is no reasons found by this court to exonerate the defendant no.1 from reducing any amount in the quantum of compensation sought by him.

35. The plaintiff sought 12% interest on the compensation, but this Court felt Rs.25 lakhs compensation sought by the plaintiff has been awarded 48 O.S.No.6869/2016 which meets the ends of justice. Thus this court felt, he is not entitled for the interest from the date of suit. But to see that the defendants shall pay the said amount within the reasonable time, thus court court felt, if she is not paid the said amount, with the time fixed by this court, the plaintiff is entitled to recover the said amount with 12% interest from the date of decree to till its realization. Thus answered issue No.3 in the affirmative and issue No.4 partly in the affirmative.

36. Issue No. 5 : As the plaintiff proved his case, which deserves to be decreed in part. thus I proceed to pass the following;

ORDER Suit of the plaintiff is decreed in part with cost.

Directed the defendant No.1 to pay Rs.25,00,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five lakhs only) as compensation to the plaintiff for causing 49 O.S.No.6869/2016 damages to his reputation, also causing mental agony, hardship in view of the defamatory complaint lodged before the Apartment Owners Association and also before the jurisdictional police.

Directed the defendant No.1 to pay the said amount within 60 days, failing which she shall pay the said amount with interest @ 12% p.a. from the date of decree to till its realization.

Office is to draw the decree accordingly. (Dictated to the Stenographer, transcript thereof corrected, signed and then pronounced by me, in open Court, on this the 31 st day of January, 2024.) case_summary: In Arvind Kejriwal vs State & Anr, the petitioner, Arvind Kejriwal, challenged the summoning order issued by the Metropolitan Magistrate, Rouse Avenue Courts, under Section 499/500 of the IPC for defamation. The case arose from a retweet by Kejriwal of a video posted by Dhruv Rathee, which allegedly contained defamatory content against the respondent, Vikas Pandey. Pandey claimed the video harmed his reputation. Kejriwal argued that retweeting did not amount to publication of defamatory content and that there was no malicious intent.
case_decision: The Delhi High Court upheld the lower court's order, holding that retweeting defamatory content constitutes publication under Section 499 IPC. The court emphasized that a retweet could spread defamatory content to a larger audience, particularly if the person retweeting has a substantial following. Kejriwal, as a public figure with a large social media reach, should have been aware of the potential reputational harm caused by retweeting the content. The petition was dismissed, and Kejriwal was required to face trial for defamation.

PRELUDE
1. The sheer magnanimity of reputational injury caused by posting defamatory content against a person who holds his reputation dear to him, which may often be dismissed as a mere tweet or retweet, has been urged to be examined, persuading this Court to adjudicate this critical issue since now the Cyber World turns Whispers into Symphony.
2. In today‟s digital age, the dynamics of law change, as exemplified by the present case, where this Court has been posed with a situation where reputational harm has been alleged by the complainant by a repost in cyberspace. In this evolving digital age, physical damage to someone‟s reputation is not the only possibility but it is the cyber world which now has taken over the real world, where if any defamatory statement is made, the effect of reputational harm is amplified. In the realm of defamation, statements made in the physical world may resemble a mere whisper, but when echoed in the cyber domain, the impact magnifies exponentially.
3. The issue before this Court through the present petition is one which requires this Court to lay down certain principles based on jurisprudence of defamation, in the light of the evolution of cyberspace, and its extensive usage as a means to damage the reputation of someone. The Court is posed with a situation where an alleged defamatory content has been posted by an original author, Signature Not Verified CRL.M.C. 6347/2019 Page 3 of 50 Digitally Signed By:ZEENAT PRAVEEN Signing Date:05.02.2024 16:25:50 and then the same content has been retweeted/reposted on the popular social media platform „Twitter‟ (now 'X') by the present petitioner.
4. While the Courts may still struggle, faced with issue as to what will amount to „publishing‟ and whether „re-tweeting‟ of a defamatory content also amounts to publishing so as to be covered under the definition of Section 499 of Indian Penal Code, 1860 ('IPC'), the concerns arising out of such vast reach of defamatory content and corresponding reputational injury to a person has given rise to the following important question of law:
Whether 'Retweeting' any defamatory content will be covered in the meaning of 'publication' or not, in terms of Section 499 of IPC & whether the act of the person 'retweeting' such content though not being the original author of the tweet, will also be liable to attract action under Section 499 of IPC or can he take refuge under the argument that he was not the original author of the content?
5. In case reported as 2017 SCC Online Delhi 1191, this Court had observed that it was for the Trial Court to decide if retweeting an allegedly defamatory content/tweet would attract rigours of Section 499 of IPC or not, by way of a full fledged trial. These observations are as under:
"26. ...Whether retweeting would attract the liability under Section 499 IPC, is a question which requires to be determined in the totality of the circumstances and the same will have to be determined during trial and any Signature Not Verified CRL.M.C. 6347/2019 Page 4 of 50 Digitally Signed By:ZEENAT PRAVEEN Signing Date:05.02.2024 16:25:50 interference at this stage by this court is likely to prejudice the findings of the Trial Court..."

6. In this background, this Court is of the opinion that whether a retweet is defamatory in content or not, so as to attract rigours of Section 499 of IPC, will of course be a matter of trial. However, whether 'Retweeting' by a person, a defamatory content, will amount to 'publication' or not so as to form the ingredient of Section 499 of IPC for the purpose of summoning of an accused, will essentially have to be decided prior to commencement of the trial. It is not the issue for adjudication before this Court in the present case to return a finding as to whether it was proved beyond doubt that the retweet in question was defamatory or not. The issue before this Court is the critical issue as to whether a retweet in itself, being not considered as original content by an original author, can form the basis of summoning an accused for offence under Section 499 of IPC.

7. This major issue being at the centre of controversy in multiple cases pending before this Court reveal the difficulties currently faced by Trial Courts in this regard and has persuaded this Court to take a comprehensive look at this issue for the purpose of summoning an accused.

BACKGROUND FACTS

8. On 06.05.2018, one Sh. Dhruv Rathee i.e. original author of the impugned/alleged defamatory content had uploaded a video on YouTube, wherein inter alia, certain allegations were made against Signature Not Verified CRL.M.C. 6347/2019 Page 5 of 50 Digitally Signed By:ZEENAT PRAVEEN Signing Date:05.02.2024 16:25:50 respondent no. 2 which has been referred to as 'First Offending Publication' in the petition. On 07.05.2018, Sh. Dhruv Rathee published on his Twitter account, an allegation that the Information and Technology („IT‟) Cell of Bharatiya Janata Party („BJP‟) had attempted to bribe a person to defame Sh. Dhruv Rathee and he had drawn a reference to Uniform Resource Locator („URL‟) of the first impugned publication, which has now been termed as 'Second Offending Publication' in the petition. On 07.05.2018, the petitioner herein, Sh. Arvind Kejriwal had reposted i.e. „retweeted‟ the second offending publication of Sh. Dhruv Rathee, which is termed as the 'Impugned Publication', and which read as under:

9. On 28.02.2019, a complaint was filed by the complainant/respondent no. 2 Sh. Vikas Sankritayan @ Vikas Signature Not Verified CRL.M.C. 6347/2019 Page 6 of 50 Digitally Signed By:ZEENAT PRAVEEN Signing Date:05.02.2024 16:25:50 Pandey, against the petitioner Sh. Arvind Kejriwal, for initiating proceedings against him for commission of offences punishable under Section 499/500 of IPC.

The Allegations

10. He alleges that Sh. "...Vikas Pandey is the Second-in-Command of the BJP IT Cell. Through his Social Media Page, "I Support Narendra Modi", which is linked by more than 1 Crore 50 Lakh people, Vikas Pandey spreads fake news.
